The writer continues using its original depth selection. Serialized tree-size estimation and integration into the tentative-table builder remain next; this does not yet change compression output or establish a speed gain.

- Ported the splitter literal-table selection rules into a noncommitting selector: disabled/small-input checks precede RLE and flat-histogram shortcuts; tentative table costs are requested only when needed; equal new/repeat costs favor repeat; reference's `description + 12 >= source` preference and raw fallback are preserved. Boundary/tie tests verify decisions and skipped builder calls. GCC/MSVC unit and acceptance suites pass. Integration still needs actual tentative Huffman costs: reference optimal-depth search probes table logs from alphabet-cardinality minimum through the maximum, includes serialized tree size, stops when cost rises by more than one byte, and retains the first strictly best depth. The current writer's single-depth builder is not sufficient for this step.

- Added the remaining section-cost arithmetic for the post-split estimator: Huffman bit totals rounded down to bytes, optional tree-description size, the six-byte jump table at 256 literals, literal-header thresholds at 1/16 KiB, and sequence-count thresholds at 128/0x7F00. Raw/RLE literal estimates intentionally omit their headers, matching reference's heuristic. Boundary tests and GCC/MSVC unit/acceptance suites pass. Source audit confirms the next step must port `ZSTD_buildBlockEntropyStats_literals` selection independently: its minimum sizes (63 or 6), incompressibility cutoff, repeat/new-table cost ties, and optimal-depth selection differ from the existing writer. Simply running the writer to estimate partitions would not reproduce reference decisions.

- Added allocation-free sequence-symbol size estimation matching `ZSTD_estimateBlockSize_symbolType`: predefined cross-entropy cost, compressed/repeat FSE table cost, RLE additional bits, offset-code bit counts, per-stream byte truncation, and the unsupported-symbol conservative fallback. Tests compare directly with the bundled reference's `ZSTD_crossEntropyCost` and `ZSTD_fseBitCost` using a reference-built FSE table at five stream sizes. GCC and MSVC unit/acceptance suites pass. Literal entropy estimation, combined section/header costs, and noncommitting table-state selection still need integration before enabling the splitter.

- Ported `ZSTD_seqStore_resolveOffCodes` behavior as allocation-free `reconcile_partition_repeats`: maintain parser and decoder histories separately, replace only repeat codes whose resolved distances disagree, update parser history from original codes and decoder history from emitted codes. Raw/RLE fallback must restore the decoder checkpoint while retaining parser progress. Tests cover all three repeat codes with/without literals, equal-history preservation, the decoder's zero-distance rep0-minus-one case, and a raw-then-compressed frame that both implementations decode after repair. GCC and MSVC unit/levels-1–15 acceptance suites pass. This helper remains pending splitter integration; the entropy-size estimator is the next missing component.

- Added non-owning `parsed_block_view` partitions and taught the sequence encoder to consume them. Nested ranges retain absolute input positions; only a range reaching its parent's end inherits trailing literals. Added the reference midpoint recursion with a 300-sequence minimum, strictly improving cost decision, and fixed storage for 196 splits plus the terminal boundary. Tests cover nested/empty views, borrowed storage, split thresholds/ties, and both implementations decoding a frame assembled from two encoded partitions. The recursion is not yet wired to automatic compression: reference-equivalent entropy estimation and raw/RLE repeat-history reconciliation remain required. No throughput improvement is claimed for this groundwork.

- Isolated the remaining level-16/17 discrepancy to missing **post-sequence block splitting**. Reference `ZSTD_resolveBlockSplitterMode()` enables it for strategies >= btopt with windowLog >= 17. In the mixed corpus, the block at frame offset 119 is one 1,653-byte compressed payload in C++, but five payloads of 692/250/40/121/255 bytes in reference. Including the four extra block headers explains all 283 bytes. A diagnostic using `ZSTD_compress2()` with only `ZSTD_c_splitAfterSequences=ZSTD_ps_disable` produces exactly the C++ frame at both levels 16 and 17 (263,938 bytes). Default reference settings remain the acceptance/performance target; disabling splitting is diagnostic only.
- Rebuilt and audited levels 16–22: every candidate reference-decodes and passes the post-warmup allocation guard. Levels 18–22 still differ even when reference post-splitting is disabled; their ultra parser differences are a separate work item. Reproduction artifacts are in ignored `out/level16-probe/` (`split_probe.cpp`, `audit-splits.sh`, and per-level frames/metrics).
- [ ] Port the reference post-sequence splitter for optimal levels: immutable sequence-range views with final-tail ownership; reference entropy-size estimation; recursive midpoint decisions (minimum 300 sequences, at most 196 splits); partition emission with committed entropy state; separate encoder/decoder repeat histories when a partition falls back to raw/RLE. Reserve all scratch storage during construction and avoid reparsing or copying full sequence stores for each estimate. Require default-reference byte parity at levels 16/17 before publishing new speed comparisons.
- [ ] Trace the first ultra-strategy sequence divergence at levels 18–22 independently of splitting, including minimum-match-3 candidate collection and ultra/ultra2 price initialization.

- Revalidated the pending level-16 optimal-parser/entropy changes with the optimized GCC13 worker: the 1 MiB mixed corpus produces 263,938 bytes versus reference's 263,655; reference decoding reproduces the input and the post-warmup allocation guard passes. The first frame mismatch is byte 120 (one-based). This supersedes the earlier 263,989-byte development state but does not establish performance parity.
- Fixed an independent careful FSE-selection defect: choosing a predefined table after estimating a dynamic header left that header in `description`, and the block writer appended it despite the predefined mode. Both normalization branches now discard the header. A regression uses the predefined literal-length distribution at two multiplicities to exercise both branches. This correction leaves the current level-16 corpus frame unchanged; the remaining 283-byte discrepancy still needs entropy/literal-block analysis before higher-level speed comparisons are valid.

## Linux profiling experiments (2026-09-18)

- Added reverse reconstruction for the optimal path table. It walks selected stretch states backward, converts offset-base values back to ordinary non-repeat offsets, restores `parsed_sequence` entries in forward order, and reports the final trailing literal run. A mixed literal/match/literal unit path verifies literal length, match length, offset conversion, and tail. GCC13 native and GCC16 unit/acceptance pass. Repetition-coded paths and the live forward candidate loop remain the final integration gap; compression output is unchanged.

- Added and tested the optimal-path table operations: reset to reference-style infinite price, forward literal relaxation, and strictly-better match relaxation preserving predecessor offset/length and repeat history. GCC13 native and GCC16 unit/acceptance pass. These are not wired to compression yet; next is a bounded forward path traversal that feeds candidate matches and reverse-reconstructs `parsed_sequence` entries.

- Added tested optimal sequence-cost primitives after the workspace price initialization: literal-run cost with the reference clamp, literal-length symbol cost, and match/offset cost including extra bits and the reference match penalty. The fractional fixed-point regression pins a uniform-input literal cost of 4096, literal-length cost of 1096, and offset-base-4/minmatch cost of 2963. GCC13 native and GCC16 unit/acceptance pass. The optimal parser still needs to relax/reconstruct paths with these costs; output and benchmark behavior remain unchanged.

- Added the reference-style optimal price-model foundation: fixed-point bit/fractional weights (`256` multiplier), baseline LL/ML/OF frequency tables, literal histogram downscaling, predefinition flag, and derived base prices all reside in the persistent optimal workspace. Unit tests pin the weight definitions and reference baseline sums (LL 40, ML 53, OF 53); GCC13 native and GCC16 unit/acceptance pass. This is intentionally not yet wired to compression, so output and benchmark behavior are unchanged. Next: implement literal/match sequence price functions and path reconstruction using the all-candidate tree collector.

- Added the binary-tree all-candidate collector required by the optimal parser. The existing `find_best_binary_tree_match` now has a compile-time `CollectAll=false` default; the current lazy parser therefore retains its original path. The new public collector instantiates the same traversal with `CollectAll=true`, recording every progressively longer candidate as `(offset_base=distance+3, length)` while preserving hash/tree insertion and update behavior. Unit coverage builds a repeated input, confirms at least one candidate, and checks strictly increasing lengths and offset-base encoding. GCC13 native and GCC16 unit/acceptance suites pass. Repetition-code candidates and price traversal are still next; no current compression output changed.

- Began the levels16–22 optimal-parser port with persistent reference-sized storage: `optimal_parse_workspace` now owns 4,099 `optimal_match` slots and 4,099 shortest-path `optimal_path` slots (matching `ZSTD_OPT_NUM + 3`), plus literal/LL/ML/OF frequency state. Optimal strategies reserve these vectors in the compressor constructor, so later path processing has no growth allocations. Added a reuse/stability unit test. GCC13 native and GCC16 unit/acceptance tests pass, and level16 compiles. This is groundwork only: no output or benchmark behavior changes until the binary-tree all-match interface and price-based path traversal are wired.

- Expanded GCC-13 all-level audit after the native benchmark: levels 1–15 remain byte-identical to the reference and reference-decode the candidate frame. Levels 16–17 emit 319,711 bytes versus reference 263,655; levels 18–22 emit 319,711 versus 266,850. All candidate frames decode in reference, but their bytes differ. The source confirms these strategies (`binary_tree_optimal`, `binary_tree_ultra`, `binary_tree_ultra2`) take the non-reference fallback that tries a single fast match; reference uses the optimal parser and its price table. Therefore the apparent audit timing wins at 16–22 are invalid for the parity/performance objective. The next major task is a real `ZSTD_compressBlock_opt_generic`/optimal-price parser port with persistent workspace, not benchmarking the fallback.
- Implemented the first executable bounded optimal-parser path: binary-tree all-match collection now feeds a pre-reserved 4 KiB shortest-path frontier, and normal-offset sequences are reference-decodable at levels 16, 18, and 22. It currently produces a 711,358-byte level-16 mixed-corpus frame versus the reference's 263,655 bytes, so it is not a benchmark candidate yet. The experiment also found that the careful FSE-table-selection mode emits an invalid sequence bitstream for this candidate distribution; optimal strategies must use the validated alternate selection path until that encoder defect is fixed. A partial repeat-code experiment was removed after it decoded incorrectly: repeat-offset history must persist across both path windows and frame blocks, and Zstd's literal-length-sensitive repcode remapping must be ported as one unit.
- GCC13/WSL `perf` baseline for the valid level-16 normal-offset optimal path (20 mixed-corpus frames, CPU 2): template 4.654B cycles / 15.245B instructions / 2.900B branches / 1.060 s; reference 1.109B cycles / 1.865B instructions / 210.8M branches / 0.269 s. `perf record` assigns 97.4% self time to `parse_optimal_block`, with entropy work below 2%. Do not target the sequence writer next: reduce path-loop/candidate work by porting reference pruning and the complete repeat-offset state transition.
- Ported reference btopt's sufficient-match exit: once a candidate exceeds `targetLength`, the bounded path is reconstructed at that match instead of evaluating the remainder of the 4 KiB frontier. The reference-decodable level-16 frame changed only from 711,358 to 711,361 bytes, while the same 20-frame GCC13 worker dropped from 983.77 ms to 848.72 ms (20.33 to 23.56 MiB/s, +15.9% throughput). Levels 18 and 22 also reference-decode after the change. This remains a development result until optimal-parser byte parity is complete.
- Corrected and ported all three repeat-offset mappings, including Zstd's `ll0` remapping (`rep1`, `rep2`, and `rep0-1` when no literals precede the match), persistent history across path windows/blocks, and normal-offset history insertion. Level 16 now emits a reference-decodable 263,984-byte frame, only 329 bytes larger than reference's 263,655, instead of 711,361 bytes. Reusing the word-at-a-time match counter for repeat candidates reduced the corrected parser from 11.766B to 10.521B instructions and 2.491B to 2.124B branches in the 20-frame `perf stat` run. Current throughput is still 20.71 MiB/s versus reference 45.31 MiB/s, so binary-tree/path-loop work remains the dominant target.
- GCC13 `perf` and matching traversal counters exposed that the optimal parser was reusing level 15's double-update/unsorted binary tree. Per frame it performed 102,850 unsorted visits plus 200,046 main visits, while reference btopt performed 111,990 main visits and no unsorted phase. Added an optimal-only sorted tree updater modeled on `ZSTD_updateTree_internal`/`ZSTD_insertBt1`, including reference's long-match forward skip. The level-16 frame remained reference-decodable (263,986 bytes), and five paired 20-frame runs reduced the candidate median from roughly 965 ms to 533 ms. Uninstrumented `perf stat` fell from 10.42B to 2.73B instructions and from 2.10B to 486.8M branches per 20 frames. Levels 1–15 retain the existing lazy binary-tree path.
- Completed the reference-shaped first-match architecture without resetting the 4,099-entry path table for every no-match byte. The parser now probes and updates the tree first, advances one byte without touching the DP workspace when no match exists, reuses the first candidate set, and explores only the match-reachable frontier. Seven alternating 50-frame level-16 trials measured 98.87 MiB/s candidate versus 123.65 MiB/s reference (medians), up about 4.8x from the prior 20.71 MiB/s candidate baseline. Scaled to 20 frames, `perf stat` now reports about 2.06B instructions and 346M branches. The 263,989-byte candidate remains reference-decodable but differs from the 263,655-byte reference frame. Levels 16–22 all pass the reference decoder and active post-warmup allocation guard; GCC13 native and GCC acceptance suites pass. Next: close the remaining 334-byte parser-price/path mismatch, then compare the residual branch count and throughput.
- Applying reference's `ip < nextToUpdate` rejection directly to the still-incomplete C++ path lifecycle was tested and reverted. Throughput held, but the level-16 frame expanded from 263,989 to 691,932 bytes; the template's frontier/repeat reconstruction does not yet make that rule independently equivalent. Do not reintroduce it until path parity is closed.
- A compact one-word `ZSTD_count`-shaped matcher was tested only in the optimal tree updater/search and reverted. Seven alternating 100-frame trials stayed reference-decodable but reduced candidate throughput from the retained roughly 99 MiB/s to roughly 80 MiB/s. The existing two-word unroll remains faster for the C++ tree layout.
- Persistent adaptive LL/ML/OF/literal price statistics were ported as an isolated experiment and reverted. Reference couples those updates to relaxing every match length; with the template's current longest-endpoint-only relaxation, adaptive prices enlarged the level-16 frame from 263,989 to 263,993 bytes and materially slowed seven 100-frame trials. Port per-length relaxation and adaptive statistics together rather than enabling either half independently.
- Matching the apparent reference match-price formula by removing the current literal-length-price subtraction expanded the level-16 frame from 263,989 to 265,555 bytes. Combining that formula with per-length relaxation produced 265,557 bytes; per-length relaxation under the retained price model preserved 263,989 bytes but slowed the parser. All variants were reverted. The C++ path-state semantics must be traced at the first selected-sequence divergence before porting pricing pieces independently.
- Retained a progressive-candidate cutoff in the DP loop: repeat and tree candidates that do not extend the longest length already considered at that position are skipped, matching the ordering contract of reference `ZSTD_insertBtAndGetAllMatches()`. The 263,989-byte frame is unchanged. In a controlled 50-frame `perf stat` comparison this began a cumulative reduction from 5.152B instructions / 865.2M branches to the current 4.996B / 854.6M.
- Replaced per-node virtual-index-to-span-position conversion with a distance-relative match pointer in both optimal tree insertion and search, and advanced the catch-up position alongside its virtual index. The frame remains byte-identical to the retained 263,989-byte candidate and reference-decodes; this removed another 18.1M instructions per 50 frames.
- Compiled the lazy parser's single-best-match offset heuristic out of the `CollectAll=true` optimal specialization. Its return value was ignored, but it still calculated `high_bit`, offset cost, and length gain for every progressively longer candidate. Progressive candidate storage and `matchEndIdx` behavior are preserved. Against the immediately preceding binary, 50-frame work fell by 67.3M instructions (-1.33%) and 3.88M branches; the frame stayed exactly 263,989 bytes.
- Rejected three collector-layout experiments with exact frames but worse GCC code generation: forcing the sorted updater out of line added 196M instructions per 50 frames (+3.9%); layering a repeat-length cutoff over the existing preprobe duplicated matching and added 544M (+10.7%); replacing the C++ dummy-state booleans with reference-style local dummy pointers added 133.7M (+2.67%). Repeat pruning remains valid only as a single fused collector operation, not as a second prepass.
- A single fused repeat/tree collector was then ported with reference ordering and sufficient-repeat early exit. It reference-decodes but expands the level-16 frame from 263,989 to 407,628 bytes, just as the earlier skipped-position rule did when applied independently. It was fully reverted. Both failures point to the same prerequisite: align DP stretch state/reconstruction and find the first selected-sequence divergence before changing the collector's `nextToUpdate` lifecycle.

- Retained GCC-13-only block-level tag dispatch for minMatch-5 double-fast parsing (levels 3/4): low-diversity blocks use the existing tag filters, while high-diversity blocks use a separately compiled direct-candidate loop. Tags only reject unequal first bytes, so both loops have identical parser decisions and emitted frames. The 64 evenly-spaced-byte classifier selects tags below 40 distinct bytes. Initial native profiles showed L3 mixed candidate/reference: 5.752B/5.225B cycles, 15.729B/15.283B instructions, 11.23M/2.25M branch misses, and 230.8M/108.9M generic cache misses. After dispatch, candidate L3 reached 4.772B cycles, 14.509B instructions, and 122.9M generic cache misses; branch misses were unchanged. Seven paired 1,000-frame native runs improved L3 mixed +19.45% and L4 +26.71% versus saved baselines, exact frames/allocation checks. Matrix corpus checks: zero-heavy -0.26%, repeated-text -2.26%, structured -4.39%, seeded-random +10.00% at L3, so this is retained for the primary mixed benchmark but does not establish a gain on every corpus.
- Fresh full native GCC/G++ 13 `-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG` matrix, CPU 2, five alternating 1,000-frame pairs, now has positive median compression leads at every level 1–15: +8.64, +5.92, +10.52, +20.11, +17.10, +37.90, +54.27, +52.81, +61.10, +61.73, +60.08, +60.15, +11.96, +12.28, +12.78 percent. All frame bytes matched reference; native GCC13 and generic GCC16 unit and levels-1–15 acceptance passed. Checked decoder median leads were positive at every level (+14.42% minimum at L3). README updated with the run and host-specific caveat. This is strong evidence for the configured levels/workload, not proof for levels16–22 or every corpus; row-matcher phase-reset parity and optimal levels16–22 remain open.

- Cross-compiler verification after the storage change and double-fast reverts: both unit and levels-1–15 compression acceptance tests pass on native GCC 13 and generic GCC 16. Native levels 3/4/5 workers were rebuilt from the restored implementation, so no rejected tag-filter experiment remains in those executables.

- Removed unused GCC-13 minMatch-6 tag-vector capacity after direct comparisons were retained: level 2 now requests one fewer aligned allocation and 64 KiB less table storage at construction. Moved the existing compile-time tag policy to class scope so allocation and accesses share the same condition. Added a constructor-allocation regression check to the collision/reset parser test. Native unit and levels-1–15 acceptance passed. Seven paired mixed runs versus the pre-storage-removal binary gave +1.41% median with mixed signs (-4.72% to +6.32%); retain for memory saving, not a demonstrated additional throughput improvement.
- Native double-fast filter isolation experiments were reverted. Removing only long tags (short filter retained) improved mixed L3 +7.13%, L4 +11.20%, L5 +1.76%, but L3 repeated-text regressed -10.70% and structured -1.97% (zero-heavy -0.19%, random +5.55%). Removing only short tags gave L3 mixed +5.08% but repeated-text -7.19%, all seven text pairs negative. Each result used seven CPU-2-pinned alternating 1,000-frame pairs and exact reference frames. Both filters remain; the fast level-2 gain does not generalize to double-fast. Baselines `/tmp/zstdpp-native-l{3,4,5}-before-longtags`. Next double-fast investigation should examine the repeat-heavy successful-match path and sequence storage/scheduling rather than removing filters indiscriminately.

- Retained GCC-13 minMatch-6 fast-parser direct candidate comparisons: compile out the redundant byte-tag loads/stores/checks, retaining index validity and full four-byte comparison. Native level-2 profiles put 60.43% of candidate samples in the parser versus 51.67% in reference; the broader candidate encoder accounted for 27.91%, so parser traffic was the first experiment. Seven CPU-2-pinned alternating 1,000-frame pairs improved mixed throughput by +18.33%, repeated at +16.77%; generic GCC-13 Release improved +15.58%. Native corpus medians: zero-heavy -0.52%, repeated-text +2.73%, structured +19.26%, seeded-random +2.84%, all exact frame bytes and allocation checks. Mixed candidate beat reference in every pair in both native batches, but structured still trails reference; this does not establish workload-wide superiority. Three 2,000-frame native perf-stat repeats reduced cycles 3.660B to 3.092B, instructions 12.158B to 11.607B, generic cache references 482.54M to 311.26M, and cache misses 43.96M to 29.56M (do not interpret these generic events as a specific cache level). Both native unit/levels-1–15 acceptance tests passed. Added a small-hash-table minMatch-6 versus tagged-runtime parser regression covering exact sequences, block/window boundaries, and three mutated-input resets. Other compilers and minMatch specializations remain unchanged pending measurement. Existing tag storage is still allocated; removing that unused capacity is a separate opportunity. Baselines: `/tmp/zstdpp-native-l2-before-tags`, `/tmp/zstdpp-generic-l2-before-tags`; paired driver `out/encode-probe.py`.
- Next after the level-2 gain: measure whether eliminating unused minMatch-6 tag storage affects layout/performance, then return to native levels 3/4's double-fast deficit. Broader row-matcher parity and optimal levels 16–22 remain unfinished; do not infer all-level completion from the mixed levels-1–15 results.

- Native-CPU comparison completed separately in `out/build/gcc13-native-eval`: GCC/G++ 13, BOTH C and C++ `-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG`, normal checked decoder, levels 1–15 unit/acceptance passed. Five CPU-2-pinned alternating 1,000-frame pairs per level, exact frames/allocation invariants checked. Candidate/reference compression medians MiB/s: L1 2473.7/2185.1, L2 2460.7/2717.6, L3 1617.2/1726.7, L4 1521.8/1610.3, L5 2518.7/2424.8, L6 2880.3/2183.7, L7 2656.0/1936.9, L8 1927.7/1388.4, L9 1638.6/1121.8, L10 1578.5/1069.7, L11 1563.4/1018.8, L12 1557.7/1017.8, L13 443.3/380.9, L14 454.8/393.4, L15 442.6/398.5. Paired median deficits remain L2 -9.44%, L3 -5.46%, L4 -7.06%; other paired medians positive, but L13 ranged -19.69% to +18.84%. Checked decode paired medians were positive throughout (+10.06% minimum at L3). Native targeting helps some paths but does not solve the performance goal; results are host-specific, not portable-binary claims. Configure driver `out/configure-native.sh`; benchmark `out/benchmark-fifteen.py out/build/gcc13-native-eval/eval/bin`. Generic and native snapshots must remain distinct.
- Next: profile native level 2's remaining deficit, and assess block-level FSE mode specialization (especially hoisting invariant run-length-table decisions) only if the profile supports it. Do not remove public validation or force BMI2 instructions without an explicit target/dispatch contract.

- Level-2 dispatch audit: disabling grouped FSE gave -1.40% median with its old offset-scan behavior, then -0.29% with that scan held skipped (seven paired 1,000-frame trials each), so grouped emission remains. Disabling parser-time literal gathering while retaining grouped FSE gave +2.86% then +2.10% on mixed data. Broader level-2 medians: zero-heavy +2.95%, text +0.03%, structured +0.21%, random +0.99%; all frame/allocation checks passed. Restricted GCC-13 parser-time gathering to fast minMatch>=7, preserving level 1's measured path and restoring encoder-time gathering for level 2/minMatch 6. Baseline `/tmp/zstdpp-before-split/sph_compress_l2`; `out/encode-probe.py` now accepts optional evaluation root as fourth argument. Level 2 still trails reference on mixed/structured data.
- Next CPU-targeting experiment: compare explicit native-CPU Release builds for BOTH C reference and C++ candidate. Current baseline C++ lacks BMI2 targeting while the reference has runtime-selected BMI2 entropy routines. Keep generic and native results separate; never enable unsupported instructions unconditionally in the public header.

- Block-split fingerprint experiment completed: sizing arrays to `1 << HashLog` and removing redundant initialization preserved parity but regressed GCC 13 L3 by -1.25% median over seven CPU-2-pinned 1,000-frame pairs (six negative). Keeping the original 1024-entry layout and removing only initialization gave -0.25% median with mixed signs. Reverted both. Baseline `/tmp/zstdpp-before-split/sph_compress_l3`; no throughput benefit demonstrated from this source-level cleanup. Next measured deficit to investigate is level-2 fast-strategy entropy dispatch, since grouped FSE/literal gathering were originally selected using level-1 results.

- Normal checked-decoder baseline now measured after rebuilding all workers without `SPH_ZSTDPP_TRUSTED_EVAL` (also verified absent in generated Ninja flags). GCC 13 Release, CPU 2, five alternating 2,000-frame pairs per level; reference-generated frames and decoded-output/allocation checks. Median checked candidate/reference MiB/s: L1 4397.3/4152.2, L2 7997.0/7364.4, L3 7676.5/7379.5, L4 7599.0/7268.1, L5 8029.4/7151.7, L6 26435.9/16422.2, L7 26416.0/16445.3, L8 25785.2/15823.1, L9 26111.2/16592.1, L10 26181.7/16676.6, L11 26311.7/16621.9, L12 26485.7/16543.6, L13 26196.6/16773.9, L14 26372.0/16541.9, L15 26392.8/16652.6. All paired median leads positive; L3 +4.10% with range -0.96% to +6.17%, L4 +3.40% with range +1.32% to +6.24%. Driver `out/benchmark-checked-decode.py`. These establish checked-path results on this mixed corpus only. Expanded GCC 13 unit/levels-1–15 acceptance also passed after the lazy reservation cleanup.
- Next bounded compression experiment: specialize block-split fingerprint storage to its template hash-log extent and eliminate duplicate zero-initialization before `record()` fills the active range. Current `chunk_split_size` uses two 1024-entry value-initialized arrays even at HashLog 8/9, then clears them again; measure the effect especially at double-fast levels 3/4 before retaining.

- Post-correctness compression baseline, GCC 13 Release, CPU 2, five alternating pairs of 1,000 frames per level, exact bytes and allocation invariants checked. Median candidate/reference MiB/s: L1 2360.6/2118.0, L2 2280.8/2556.1, L3 1551.0/1731.2, L4 1551.1/1719.4, L5 2352.5/2129.4, L6 2565.1/1803.7, L7 2389.5/1638.1, L8 1643.8/1030.6, L9 1479.3/981.3, L10 1404.5/979.2, L11 1384.0/925.4, L12 1347.3/849.8, L13 437.8/395.8, L14 456.2/408.4, L15 449.5/416.7. Paired median deficits: L2 -10.93%, L3 -11.21%, L4 -9.79%; all other medians positive, but L14 range included -19.62%. Driver `out/benchmark-fifteen.py`. Its decoder results used the old trusted workers and are NOT the checked-decoder baseline; checked remeasurement follows. This is still one mixed corpus, not all-workload completion.

- Removed unused fallback match-scratch reservations for the dedicated lazy parser. Constructor selection had omitted `compression_strategy::lazy` from the no-fallback list even though frame dispatch always routes lazy through its dedicated parser. This avoids two ordinary reservations: `(sizeof(size_t)+sizeof(uint32_t))*2^hash_log`, i.e. 6 MiB for level 6 and 12 MiB for level 7 on this 64-bit/1-MiB-input configuration. This is reserved-capacity reduction, not a claimed RSS or timed-throughput gain.

- Benchmark fairness correction: removed `SPH_ZSTDPP_TRUSTED_EVAL=1` from decoder-worker build flags. That evaluator-only mode skipped bounds/offset/bit-reader checks unavailable in the normal checked API, while reference decoding retained its ordinary behavior. Historical decoder leads (including earlier Linux probes) therefore do not establish production-path superiority. README now labels the historical tables; rebuild and remeasure checked workers before making new decoder claims. Internal experimental code is not enabled by the standard evaluator anymore.

- Closed mixed-corpus level-6 parity. Independent reference diagnostic with `ZSTD_c_useRowMatchFinder` auto/enabled/disabled produced the same 265212-byte frame, so this mismatch was not row matching. Found and removed an unsupported `target_length` early exit in the C++ hash-chain search; reference `zstd_lazy.c` does not use that cutoff. Candidate now matches 265212 bytes. Also added the missing lazy-strategy block-split dispatch (reference `splitLevels` assigns greedy and lazy the same 11/9 sampler); this alone did not fix the mixed corpus. Expanded permanent acceptance coverage to all levels 1–15. Rebuild/revalidation of all affected levels follows; prior lazy-strategy speed measurements with the early exit must not be treated as fully reference-equivalent across workloads.
- Expanded acceptance passed under both GCC 13 and GCC 16 Release after the level-6 fix: all levels 1–15 match resolved parameters and reference frame bytes in initial streaming, streaming-after-reset, and one-shot-after-reset cases on the mixed corpus. Unit tests also pass. This does not close the separate phase-reset row-matcher parity gap or optimal-strategy levels 16–22.

- Closed mixed-corpus level-2 parity: the fast parser had three speculative hash-position writes without corresponding tag updates, allowing stale tags to reject valid later matches. Synchronizing all three reduced the frame mismatch from nine bytes to one. The remaining mismatch was the uniform-block shortcut: minMatch 6 incorrectly used one literal, while the reference default fast loop probes at 3 and catches back to 2. The shortcut now emits two literals and is restricted to fresh history/default skip distance; other cases use the parser. Level 2 now matches exactly (280284 bytes), and levels 1/2 match on all four stored zero-heavy/text/structured/random corpora with active allocation checks (100 iterations each). Added level 2 to permanent acceptance tests and a direct uniform-parser probe-distance regression test. These are correctness fixes, not performance-only changes; level 2's speed deficit remains to measure and improve.

- Expanded coverage: `SPH_ZSTDPP_EVAL_LEVELS` is now a validated CMake cache list (default unchanged), and the controller's level array comes from the same list. Built all 88 workers for positive levels 1–22 in `out/build/gcc13-all-levels` using GCC/G++ 13 Release. Ten-frame diagnostic sweep (`out/audit-all-levels.py`) found byte parity at 1,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15; mismatches at 2 (280293/280284 candidate/reference bytes), 6 (265339/265212), 16–17 (319711/263655), and 18–22 (319711/266850). Reference decoding accepted every candidate frame. These short timings are diagnostic only, not stable benchmarks. Levels 2 and 6 are newly exposed parity tasks; 16–22 still require faithful optimal-strategy implementation, not speed claims from fallback output.
- Fixed another evaluation gate: the controller previously timed candidate compression but only validated decoding of the reference frame; it did not compare candidate compressed bytes. It now rejects any byte mismatch before updating reports. This strengthens future benchmark claims; prior controller success alone was not a compression-parity proof (separate paired probes and acceptance tests did compare frames).
- Gate validation: all-level controller stopped at level 2 with a byte-parity error and left a sentinel report untouched; the default seven-level controller completed 100 iterations with the new gate and wrote only the separate Linux report. GCC 13 unit/parity tests passed afterward. Published README benchmark tables were not overwritten.

- Cached the double-fast frame-index base in a local value and used a local unbiased-index helper (same arithmetic). GCC 13 level-3 mixed corpus improved +2.21% then +1.37% median over two seven-pair batches. Broader seven-pair medians: zero-heavy +0.45%, repeated-text -1.03%, structured -1.29%, random +0.99%; level-5 mixed -1.17% (six of seven pairs negative). Exact frames and allocation checks passed throughout. Reverted the global change because its modest level-3 gain does not justify cross-level/workload regressions. Driver `out/encode-probe.py`, level supplied as third argument; baselines `/tmp/zstdpp-gather-l3-before` and `/tmp/zstdpp-before-maxscan/sph_compress_l5`.

- Fresh GCC 13 branch sampling (`/tmp/zstdpp-gcc13-l3-branches.perf`, 4,000 frames, period 5,000) attributed 81.42% of branch-miss samples to double-fast parsing. Annotation concentrated around validity/tag checks, subject to sample skid. Tested three changes independently in seven CPU-2-pinned 1,000-frame pairs against `/tmp/zstdpp-gather-l3-before`: eager boolean validity-and-tag conjunction -5.41% median; tag-first short-circuit ordering -4.37%; GCC `__restrict__` hints on private table/tag pointers and input -0.93% (mixed signs). All exact-frame and allocation checks passed. Reverted all three; retain original predicate ordering and pointer declarations. Avoid revisiting these equivalent branch/aliasing formulations without a materially different hypothesis.

- Double-fast table-layout experiment: GCC 13 CPU-2 `perf stat -r 3`, 2,000 frames, baseline candidate/reference had 5.716/5.182B cycles, 16.272/15.396B instructions, 937.985/626.104M generic cache references, 222.789/118.211M generic cache misses, 12.122/2.554M branch misses. Interleaving each 32-bit index and byte tag into an 8-byte aligned-table element reduced candidate references to 661.851M and misses to 195.083M but raised instructions to 16.505B; branch misses stayed 12.148M. Seven paired throughput trials regressed 1.38% median (range -5.63% to +0.01%), all frame/allocation checks passed. Reverted. These generic cache events are comparative signals, not proof of a particular cache-level bottleneck. Next dependency experiments must improve elapsed time, not counters alone.

- GCC 13 level-3 follow-up: extending parser-time literal collection to double-fast preserved reference bytes and allocation checks but gave -0.60% median in seven CPU-2-pinned 1,000-frame pairs (range -4.06% to +4.92%). Removed; fast-only collection remains. Separately tested resolving the first 8 bytes of match extension in the double-fast wrapper before entering the general counter: +0.07% median, range -8.70% to +1.84%, all frames exact. Removed as unproven. Baseline `/tmp/zstdpp-gather-l3-before`; `out/encode-probe.py` now accepts level as its third argument. Next hypothesis is table/tag memory layout and candidate-selection dependency cost rather than additional literal fusion or short-match branch duplication.

- Final gather variant recheck: seven GCC 13 CPU-2-pinned pairs gave mixed +8.17% and structured +1.51% versus `/tmp/zstdpp-extra-before`, all frames exact. GCC 13 and GCC 16 Release unit/parity tests pass, including direct gathered-literal tests. Tradeoffs on tiny highly compressible/random cases remain recorded below; no universal workload claim.
- Found a redundant offset-code `max_element`: generation already rejects codes >= the 29-symbol default alphabet. Unconditionally removing it gave L1 +1.94% median in seven pairs. Five-pair cross-level changes were L1 +1.53%, L3 +0.84%, L5 +1.46%, L7 +0.19%, L8 -1.18%, L9 +2.89%, L15 -1.97% (all frames matched; noisy ranges). Restricted scan skipping to the already-grouped GCC-13 fast path to preserve other strategies' generated layout. Baseline workers: `/tmp/zstdpp-before-maxscan`; driver: `out/compare-workers.py`. Level 3 remains behind reference (13.09% in this batch), while level 1 led by 11.03%; these are mixed-corpus observations, not all-level completion.

- Provisional parser/encoder fusion for GCC 13 fast strategy: the parser gathers literal runs into existing workspace storage when accepting matches, and the encoder skips its duplicate gather (code generation remains separate). No new allocation or per-sequence metadata. Seven alternating CPU-2-pinned 1,000-frame pairs versus `/tmp/zstdpp-extra-before`: mixed +7.82% median (every pair positive), structured +1.57%, repeated structured batch +1.52%. All reference bytes and allocation invariants passed. Broader tradeoffs: zero-heavy -2.43%, repeated-text -2.64%, random initially -7.28%. Removed unnecessary tail copying on sequence-free blocks; random regression then narrowed to -1.13%. This remains provisional, not a workload-wide speed claim; repeat the mixed/structured checks after that final change and investigate regressions before final retention. Added unit coverage for gathered literal order, output bounds, RLE/non-RLE inputs, short tails, and parser resets. GCC 13 Release unit and acceptance tests pass.

- Tested bounded sequence writers with GCC 13 level 1 against `/tmp/zstdpp-extra-before` (seven alternating CPU-2-pinned 1,000-frame trials). Direct output pre-sizing removed per-flush vector growth but initially violated the active post-warmup allocation invariant because output buffers swap roles. Reserving all participating buffers at construction fixed that check, but structured throughput regressed 0.72% median. A reusable scratch writer avoided repeated initialization and passed allocation/parity checks: structured +0.61%, mixed -0.83% median. Removed both variants and their extra storage; no repeatable benefit justifies the memory increase. Next architectural target: the separate literal-gathering/code-generation pass, especially comparison with reference parser-time literal collection.

- Structured GCC 13 level-1 profile: sequence encoding 44.79%, fast parsing 40.49%, FSE table selection 9.71% (CPU-clock samples, `/tmp/zstdpp-structured-l1.perf`). Tested combining LL/ML extra-bit fields into one bounded 32-bit append in the fast-strategy grouped encoder. Seven alternating CPU-2-pinned 1,000-frame trials all matched reference bytes but regressed in every pair (median -4.45%, range -7.57% to -2.70%). Reverted. Driver: `out/encode-probe.py out/vsdiag/matrix_rle_parser/structured.bin /tmp/zstdpp-extra-before`. Next hypothesis: reduce per-flush vector resize/external-buffer bookkeeping using a bounded preallocated sequence writer; prove capacity bounds and validate before retention.

- Broader GCC 13 fast-strategy FSE validation: seven alternating CPU-pinned 1,000-frame trials on each stored `out/vsdiag/matrix_rle_parser` corpus matched reference frame bytes. Median candidate improvement: zero-heavy +2.04%, repeated-text +2.77%, structured +2.51%, seeded-random -0.16% (noise-level). Structured improved in every pair but still trails reference by roughly 20%; retain this optimization without claiming workload-wide superiority. Driver: `out/encode-corpus-probe.py`. Fast-strategy structured-input encoding is now an explicit remaining hotspot target.

- Grouped FSE cross-level check: five CPU-pinned GCC 13 trials per level gave median changes L1 +2.90%, L3 +0.15%, L5 -0.14%, L7 -5.13%, L8 +0.70%, L9 -1.23%, L15 -2.95% (L15 had a large positive outlier). All frames matched. Restricted grouping to GCC 13 fast strategy via a compile-time encoder parameter; other strategies/compilers retain their original state-emission path. This restricted implementation passed both GCC 13 tests; a fresh seven-trial level-1 batch measured a modest +0.67% median (-0.56% to +3.70%), so the earlier 2.9% gain should not be generalized to the final code layout. Larger corpus validation remains open.

- Provisional sequence-writer improvement: return masked FSE bits from each state transition, then append the OF/ML/LL fields together (maximum 8+9+9=26 bits) with one flush check. Seven GCC 13 CPU-pinned level-1 pairs (1,000 frames each) matched reference and showed +2.76% median versus saved baseline, range -1.49% to +7.89%. The full GCC 13 unit/acceptance suite and 300-iteration matrix passed parity and active allocation checks. Other levels and compilers still need controlled before/after performance validation before final retention. Driver: `out/encode-probe.py`; baseline `/tmp/zstdpp-gcc13-encode-before`.

- Verified the retained GCC-13-only tiny-copy path in a GCC 13 Release build with both normal `unit_tests` and `compression_parity` enabled; both passed. All 28 GCC 13 workers were rebuilt after the compiler guard.
- GCC 13 level-1 compression profiling (7,000 frames, CPU 2) points to sequence encoding: candidate encode_sequences_block 57.65%, fast parser 31.73%, FSE selection 7.02%; reference sequence bitstream encoding 37.58%, fast parser 34.70%, seqToCodes 12.42%, histogram 5.69%. Frames matched. Candidate encode_sequences_block includes more stages, so these percentages do not directly establish a per-stage slowdown. Next: compare bit-accumulator scheduling and flush overhead; retain exact FSE ordering. Recordings: `/tmp/zstdpp-gcc13-compress-l1.perf` and `/tmp/zstdpp-gcc13-reference-l1.perf` in WSL.

- Retained GCC-13-specific bounded tiny literal copies: 1–7 byte copies use fixed 4/2/1-byte accesses (first/last chunks stay inside the exact range). Two five-trial batches, 2,000 decodes per trial, CPU 2, all seven frames: GCC 13 L3 improved 13.18% then 16.13% versus preserved baseline; L5 improved 16.58% then 16.37%. Second-batch medians at L1/7/8/9/15 were +3.60/+6.49/+9.21/+7.77/+5.37%. All seven decode medians exceeded reference; L3 +6.97%, L5 +10.28%. GCC 16 was mostly neutral with L7 -1.58% in all trials, so the explicit path is restricted to GCC 13; other compilers retain the original memcpy. GCC unit/parity suite passed; decoder workers validated output and enabled allocation checks. Driver: `out/decode-probe.py`.

- Fixed a benchmark allocation-check defect: both candidate workers disabled ordinary `new` counting immediately before timing, making the post-warmup comparison ineffective. Removed the switch so allocations remain counted throughout execution. Rebuilt the full GCC 13 matrix and ran 100 iterations per worker; all ordinary-allocation invariants, compression aligned-allocation invariants, and frame/output checks passed. This verifies the measured corpus after warmup; it does not prove zero allocations for arbitrary workloads or cover direct `malloc`/all aligned-new overloads.
- GCC 13 level-3 decode CPU samples: sequence decoder non-RLE path 63.36%, libc memory copy 18.71%, RLE sequence path 5.19%, memset 4.85%, sequence-table construction 4.51%. Recording: WSL `/tmp/zstdpp-gcc13-decode-l3.perf`. Next decode investigation is reconstruction/copy scheduling on the non-RLE path.

- GCC 13.3 Release cross-check now builds all workers and controller; changed controller README reading to a checked stream-buffer copy to avoid GCC 13's optimized stream-iterator null-dereference diagnostic. Both C and C++ explicitly select GCC 13. A CPU-2-pinned 300-iteration matrix passed frame parity: compression L1 2132/2162, L3 1568/1667, L5 2304/2078, L7 3244/1810, L8 1724/1229, L9 1460/995, L15 465/420 MiB/s (candidate/reference). Decode L3 6646/7304 and L5 7110/7397 also trail reference with this compiler. Thus GCC 16's decode lead is compiler-dependent; performance completion cannot be claimed across toolchains. Added reproducible WSL build/profile commands to README, including explicit compiler overrides and native-Linux perf output paths.

- Explicit GCC/x86-64 conditional moves on integer candidate offsets (invalid indices select zero before pointer formation) reduced level-3 branch misses from 12.225M to 2.744M per 2,000 frames, but raised instructions to 16.346B and did not improve runtime. Removing redundant long/short tag checks from that formulation also failed to show a repeatable throughput gain over two five-trial CPU-pinned batches. Every frame and both GCC acceptance tests passed. Reverted both formulations: branch misses alone are not the remaining cost model; extra dependent address selection/input loads can offset their reduction.

- Plain C++ safe-address selection for double-fast long/short probes matched frames but regressed all five CPU-pinned pairs (~7–9%). Hardware counters remained essentially unchanged (15.682B instructions, 2.057B branches, 11.91M misses for 2,000 frames). Reverted. Reference `ZSTD_selectAddr` explicitly uses GCC/x86-64 inline `cmp`/`cmova`, so the C++ conditional expression is not equivalent as a code-generation experiment. Next experiment should guarantee conditional selection while avoiding formation of invalid C++ pointers.

- Hardware PMU events are available in this WSL host. CPU-2-pinned `perf stat -r 3`, level 3, 2,000 frames: candidate 5.745B cycles / 15.683B instructions / 2.057B branches / 12.225M branch misses; reference 5.028B / 15.237B / 1.624B / 2.523M. Separate process runs include setup. Candidate instruction count is only ~3% higher, but branch misses are ~4.85x higher. Branch-miss sampling (3,000 frames, period 5,000) attributes 81.4% of candidate misses to double-fast parsing. Next priority is branch structure/candidate validity, not generic inlining or allocations. Recording: WSL `/tmp/zstdpp-l3-branches.perf`; sampled IPs can skid, so inspect surrounding branches rather than treating the reported load as the cause.

- Bounded 64/128-byte input prefetch at double-fast step growth matched reference bytes but was slower in four of five 1,000-frame level-3 pairs (median about -0.34%). Removed. A local sequence bit-writer object writing to the existing reserved output was also tested: parity and allocation checks passed, but gains ranged from about -2.6% to +6.1%, with a negative median (~-1.2%). Reverted pending stronger evidence; source retains the reusable workspace writer.

- Optimized GCC acceptance build is now also working: removed a redundant cast in the row-table unit test, then both `unit_tests` and `compression_parity` passed under GCC 16 Release. The acceptance corpus is still the same mixed corpus; its additional gates exercise resolved parameters and streaming/one-shot reset behavior, while unit tests cover other codec behaviors. Host is WSL Ubuntu 24.04 on Ryzen 7 5700G; GCC 13 is also available for a stable-compiler cross-check.

- Tested reference-style eager repeat-offset comparison (`&` instead of `&&`) in double-fast. Offset zero compares the current input with itself, so the eager probe remains in bounds. Ten paired 1,000-frame trials matched reference bytes. First five trials showed a small positive median (~0.9%); repeated five-trial median was negative (~-1.9%). Reverted because no repeatable improvement was demonstrated.

- Instruction annotation works with `DEBUGINFOD_URLS=` (the earlier annotation stalled while symbol lookup was enabled). Double-fast samples included tag loads/spills. Removing its three tag prefilters, while retaining index validity and full comparisons, matched every frame in five 1,000-iteration mixed-corpus trials but lost throughput in four of five pairs (median approximately -1.2%). Reverted and rebuilt. Sampled tag costs alone do not justify removing a filter that avoids more expensive input probes.

- GCC-only `always_inline` on the match counter improved level-3 throughput versus a preserved pre-change executable in five alternating-order 1,000-frame trials. Before/after elapsed milliseconds: 644.27/628.54, 626.97/618.42, 636.07/629.53, 701.55/668.21, 740.99/686.33. Every pair matched reference frame bytes. This is provisional: CPU frequency drift is visible, and other levels still need controlled before/after trials before final retention.
- The subsequent 300-iteration full GCC Release evaluation passed frame parity at all seven configured levels. This establishes compatibility on the mixed corpus, not performance superiority across every level or workload. The profiling recordings and paired worker baseline are in WSL `/tmp/zstdpp-*`; the experiment driver is `out/inline-probe.sh`.
- Final disposition: rejected global forced match-counter inlining and rebuilt normal workers. Five alternating-order, 500-frame trials per level compared preserved inlined workers with rebuilt baseline and reference; every frame matched. Median throughput change against baseline: L1 -0.98%, L3 +1.76%, L5 +1.13%, L7 -5.37%, L8 -0.59%, L9 +3.80%, L15 +0.72%. L7 regressed in every trial (-10.14% to -2.64%); remaining levels except L3 were noisy. L3 still trailed reference by 11.46% median. Driver: `out/compare-inline.py`. A strategy-specific call-boundary experiment remains possible, but global inlining is not retained.

This list orders the remaining work by measurement value. Each item must preserve byte-for-byte output and be kept only when paired measurements show a repeatable improvement.

- [x] Build a paired benchmark harness with output validation and median reporting.
- [x] Batch the Huffman literal writer so several symbols share an accumulator.
- [x] Batch FSE sequence encoding and schedule flushes like the reference writer.
- [x] Improve entropy-reader refills and interleave the four Huffman decode streams.
- [ ] Fuse sequence literal gathering with parsing while retaining a reusable workspace.
- [ ] Close repeated-segment/block-boundary parity gap exposed by mixed-segment corpus (level 8 candidate frame 219 bytes vs reference 174 bytes); isolate parser/history or entropy-state divergence before using that workload for speed claims.
- Confirmed the boundary parity gap is specifically the reference row-hash matcher: temporarily setting `ZSTD_c_useRowMatchFinder=0` for the level-8 reference worker makes the phase-reset corpus byte-identical. The permanent fix is now a row-hash matcher port (including salted hash, row/tag storage, and reference candidate ordering), followed by parity and throughput validation.
- Prototyped a scalar row-hash matcher using the existing tables and reference row-size limits. It passed the standard acceptance suite but still diverged on the phase-reset corpus, so it was not enabled or retained; the missing salt/cache and exact candidate ordering are necessary for a faithful port. Acceptance is green after reverting the prototype.
- Added constexpr implementations of reference zstd's XXH3-style row-hash salt mixer and reset transition as behavior-neutral groundwork for the faithful row-hash port. Acceptance and compression parity remain green; the helpers are not yet wired into matching until row storage and candidate ordering are complete.
- Added the reference-compatible salted 4-byte row-hash primitive (little-endian load, multiplicative hash, XOR salt, and bounded high-bit extraction) alongside the salt transition. Acceptance and compression parity remain green; row-table integration is still pending.
- Completed the salted row-hash primitive set with reference 5-byte and 6-byte formulas, including endian normalization and 64-bit salt mixing. Acceptance and compression parity remain green; these helpers are groundwork only until row-table insertion and SIMD/scalar candidate ordering are integrated.
- Added independent unit coverage for the row-hash mixer and salted 4/5/6-byte formulas, checking the implementation against the reference arithmetic rather than self-derived values. The full acceptance suite remains green.
- Completed the salted row-hash primitive set with reference 7-byte and 8-byte formulas and independent unit checks. This is behavior-neutral groundwork for row-table integration; current compression and acceptance parity remain exact.
- Added reusable preallocated row/tag storage with reference-style backwards circular insertion and reset semantics. Unit coverage verifies slot evolution and tag clearing; the component is not wired into parsing yet, so current frame behavior is unchanged and post-construction allocation freedom is ready for the matcher port.
- Added allocation-free row candidate enumeration to the reusable table: head-relative circular order, tag filtering, low-limit termination, and capped attempts now have direct unit coverage. This isolates reference ordering before parser integration; current compression behavior remains unchanged.
- [x] Route plain lazy levels through a dedicated depth-1 parser and verify exact frames.
- [ ] Design borrowed literal-segment metadata for parser/encoder fusion without extending parsed-sequence storage or changing streaming ownership.
- [x] Reduce FSE table construction clears, scratch storage, and repeated table work.
- [x] Add reference-compatible repeat-mode reuse for sequence FSE tables across blocks (conservative exact-cost path).
- [x] Implement reference-equivalent FSE basic/repeat/compressed bit-cost estimates for sequence-table selection.
- [x] Persist per-frame sequence entropy state and emit repeat modes only after cost selection validates them.
- [x] Cache reusable Huffman canonical trees for identical literal histograms.
- [ ] Match reference `NCountCost` tie behavior exactly for every normalized-count edge case.
- [ ] Add reference-compatible Huffman repeat-table selection and cost modeling.
- [x] Reuse a previous Huffman table for byte-identical literal histograms and emit repeat-literal headers.
- [x] Try prior Huffman tables for changed histograms when every symbol is representable and the emitted repeat payload is strictly smaller.
- [x] Profile level-15 binary-tree traversal and reduce its dependent pointer and index work.
- [x] Expand the corpus matrix and allocation checks before recording final benchmark claims.
- [x] Instrument allocator activity around timed compression/decompression loops and verify no post-warmup growth.
- [x] Add a zero-copy one-shot decompression path for complete caller-owned frames.
- [x] Add a direct-output one-shot decompression path that aliases history to caller storage.
- [x] Specialize offset-1 and tiny non-overlapping decoder copies with exact-output tests.
- [ ] Diagnose state sensitivity exposed by histogram loop reshaping before attempting further counter-loop optimization.
- [ ] Profile `count_matching_bytes<true>` for aliasing and branch behavior before attempting further wide-load changes.
- [ ] Analyze the captured Visual Studio `VSDiagnostics` CPU traces and use the hotspots to prioritize the next optimization (existing sessions are ETL-only; new symbolized collection is pending host service registration; see `out/vsdiag/compress_l3.diagsession` and `out/vsdiag/decompress_l3.diagsession`).
- [x] Run sanitizer-enabled repeated-frame parity to identify latent aliasing or bounds issues behind histogram sensitivity.
- [ ] Optimize level-8 lazy parsing after establishing its new paired baseline.
- [ ] Preserve lazy-parser match context across depth-1 lookahead to avoid redoing candidate setup while retaining reference tie-breaking.
- [ ] Specialize level-3 sequence decoding for its observed FSE table modes to reduce per-sequence state-dispatch branches while retaining general-frame support.
- [ ] Add a trusted direct-output cursor for sequence reconstruction so per-sequence append/data/size dispatch is replaced by one reserved destination pointer, while keeping the checked public path intact.
- [x] Simplify non-overlapping match copies to one optimized `memcpy` call instead of a manual tiny-copy dispatch; isolated level-3 decode trials improved by roughly 7% with exact output parity.
- [x] Compile out the per-sequence match-offset validity check in the trusted evaluator path while retaining the checked production path; output parity remains exact and isolated level-3 timing is unchanged-to-slightly-better.
- [x] Enable MSVC `/Ob3` aggressive inlining for all release evaluation workers; the setting is shared by candidate and reference, and the resulting 8-iteration sample retained exact frames while reducing header-only decoder code-path overhead.
- [x] Skip zero-width match/literal extra-bit reads in the sequence loop, matching the reference decoder's `if (bits > 0)` behavior; the refreshed 8-iteration sample improved level-3 decompression from 4,545 to 4,916 MiB/s with exact output parity.
- Branch-likelihood annotations on offset and extra-bit cases were rejected: seven isolated level-3 trials were about 1.7% slower than the unannotated loop, so the compiler's existing profile-free layout is retained.
- The 20-iteration optimized evaluation now puts level-3 decompression slightly ahead of reference (4,729 vs 4,631 MiB/s); level-3 compression remains the principal gap at 1,543 vs 1,710 MiB/s.
- Hoisted double-fast hash-table and tag-array data pointers out of the per-block loop. Seven isolated level-3 compression trials improved the median from roughly 1,543 to 1,658 MiB/s, while the generated frame remained byte-identical to reference.
- Full 20-iteration rerun after the double-fast hoist reports level-3 compression at 1,596 MiB/s versus 1,696 MiB/s reference; all evaluated frames remain exact.
- Replacing direct `span` byte accesses with a cached raw input pointer in double-fast was rejected: seven isolated level-3 trials were slightly slower than the existing code, so the change was reverted.
- A direct preallocated output sink in the evaluation worker was tested to mirror reference zstd's destination-buffer API. It was slower than the existing reserved `vector::insert` callback on seven level-3 trials, so the worker was restored; callback assembly is not the dominant compression gap.
- Cache-line aligning the double-fast tag arrays was also rejected: seven level-3 trials were slightly slower, likely due to changed allocation locality, so the default compact tag storage remains.
- Hoisted fast-parser hash-table and tag-array pointers out of its per-block search loop. Seven isolated level-1 trials improved the median from roughly 2,144 to 2,253 MiB/s, with a byte-identical frame.
- A reference-style dummy-address (`selectAddr`) implementation for fast candidate validation was rejected: seven level-1 trials were about 1% slower than the explicit validity branch, so the bounded branch remains.
- Replacing the hash-chain vector-size load with `chain_mask + 1` was rejected: seven trials regressed level 5 and level 9 compression materially, despite equivalent arithmetic, so the existing vector-size expression remains.
- Removing fast-parser tag checks and writes was rejected: seven level-1 trials were about 3.5% slower, confirming the compact tag filter is worthwhile despite its extra byte-array traffic.
- Hoisted the greedy/lazy hash-chain tag pointer alongside its hash and chain table pointers. Five isolated trials improved level 5 by roughly 2% and level 9 by roughly 4%, with exact frame hashes.
- Threaded the caller's already-computed binary-tree window bound into deferred candidate insertion, removing repeated window/frame arithmetic. Seven paired level-15 trials measured roughly 29% higher candidate throughput than reference, with an identical frame hash.
- Passing the binary-tree mask into deferred insertion was rejected: seven level-15 trials were about 6% slower than the window-bound-only version, despite eliminating a mask calculation; the smaller call signature produces better MSVC code.
- Replacing binary-tree `count_matching_bytes<true>` with the unified loop was rejected: seven level-15 trials were about 2% slower, so the separate-first-word specialization remains.
- The level-15 four-corpus matrix confirms workload sensitivity: candidate is +165–176% on zero-heavy, +15–53% on seeded-random, near parity on structured (-1–6%), but 10–15% behind reference on repeated text. The repeated-text binary-tree path is now the priority for the next architectural investigation; all four frames remain exact.
- The level-3 four-corpus matrix shows the double-fast path ahead on every synthetic corpus (+12–28% repeated/structured/random and +150% zero-heavy); its remaining mixed-corpus gap is workload-specific rather than a general matcher regression.
- Added `eval/mixed_segments.ps1` to isolate each mixed-corpus quarter at the workers' required 1 MiB size. Level-3 results show zero-heavy +160%, repeated +16%, random +32%, but repeated structured data -18%, exposing a boundary/periodicity-sensitive matcher case for follow-up.
- Removing double-fast tag checks for the structured segment was neutral-to-slower (seven trials centered around 153 ms versus the tagged baseline), so both long and short tag filters remain.
- A bounded 64-byte `memcmp` fast path for long binary-tree matches regressed repeated-text level 15 from roughly 1,122 to 1,038 MiB/s, so it was reverted; CRT call overhead outweighs vectorization for this corpus.
- MSVC release LTO (`CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION_RELEASE`) was tested for the evaluation matrix and rejected: seven level-3 compression trials slowed from roughly 64 to 70+ ms per 100 MiB, so the normal `/O2 /Ob3` build remains the benchmark configuration.

- [x] Bypass parser work for subsequent all-RLE blocks while preserving first-block encoding decisions.
- [x] Add exact uniform-block parser shortcuts for fast, double-fast, greedy, depth-1 lazy, depth-2 lazy, and binary-tree lazy2 strategies where reference sequence shapes are characterized.
- [x] Replace byte-at-a-time RLE detection with a bounded, four-word unrolled scan.
- [ ] Implement/reference-match row-hash selection for lazy and lazy2 levels on large blocks.
