- [ ] Row-hash subtask: port row update and candidate enumeration with reference ordering (reusable SIMD table primitive is complete; production parser integration remains open).
- [ ] Row-hash subtask: validate exact frames and benchmark against the chain matcher by corpus.
- [x] Re-run the corpus matrix after restoring correct tag validity semantics in fast/double-fast matchers.
- [x] Profile repeated-text binary-tree traversal against reference's `ZSTD_bt_findBestMatch` and identify the extra candidate visits or state updates before changing frame-producing behavior.
- [x] Add zero-overhead-off-by-default binary-tree counters for unsorted catch-up visits, main-tree visits, and match-length extensions; compare them with an equivalently instrumented reference worker before altering traversal semantics.
- [x] Split mixed-corpus timing by block regime (RLE, text, structured, random) and quantify parser reset, sequence-table setup, and callback costs independently.
- [x] Add opt-in phase timing for parser, sequence/entropy encoding, and output emission in the compression worker; use it to explain optimized level-15 cost after traversal counts are proven identical.
- [ ] Add equivalent phase timing around the reference compressor's binary-tree search and block encoding to compare stage costs directly.
- Reworked the single-match fallback encoder used by the higher/optimal strategies to consume the persistent compression workspace. Literal gathering, raw-literal framing, Huffman output, and sequence extra-bit writing now reuse reserved buffers instead of allocating temporary vectors per candidate block; the standalone helper retains its original ownership behavior. Acceptance and optimized workers build cleanly, with the allocation invariant preserved. A dedicated benchmark for the optimal-strategy fallback remains queued.
- A first integrated scalar row-table attempt was rejected after the standard acceptance suite passed but the repeated-text phase-reset corpus still produced a byte mismatch. The partial implementation is fully reverted; row-hash storage and candidate ordering remain a correctness-gated task, not an enabled optimization.
- Tightened the workspace-backed single-match fallback further by replacing iterator-based vector inserts with sized `memcpy` copies. This keeps the path allocation-free after warmup and reduces range/iterator overhead; acceptance and compression-parity tests remain exact. Throughput on an optimal-strategy corpus is still needed before claiming a measurable gain.
- Temporarily added a level-16 paired worker to exercise the fallback path. It immediately failed byte parity because the template does not yet implement reference zstd's binary-tree-optimal strategy; the temporary target was removed. This confirms that fallback allocation work is future-facing, while the current validated performance matrix remains levels 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, and 15.
- Refreshed the optimized 20-iteration matrix after the workspace-copy cleanup. All published frames remain byte-identical; the timing snapshot is workload-sensitive but records candidate compression ahead at levels 3 (1,567 vs 1,213 MiB/s), 7 (2,579 vs 1,019), 8 (1,862 vs 1,628), 9 (2,198 vs 1,474), and 15 (751 vs 575), with level 1 near parity and level 5 near parity. This does not isolate the fallback path because levels 1–15 do not use it.
- Outlined the level-15 binary-tree search on MSVC with `__declspec(noinline)`, matching reference zstd's outlined search wrapper and reducing parser-loop code pressure. Exact frames remain unchanged; five mixed repeated-text trials reached +0.74% median and a longer nine-trial/500-iteration probe reached +0.68% (range -20.67% to +5.01%, one scheduler outlier), moving the stable median from roughly 8% behind to parity. Structured mixed text remained near parity (-3.95% in the five-trial check).
- Refreshed the full optimized matrix after retaining binary-tree outlining. Exact frame bytes remain equal; the 20-iteration snapshot records candidate compression at level 3 (1,630 vs 1,811 MiB/s), level 5 (2,329 vs 2,024), level 7 (3,553 vs 1,508), level 8 (1,643 vs 1,233), level 9 (1,589 vs 1,181), and level 15 (803 vs 659). This confirms the level-15 gain survives the broad run while level 3 remains the principal published compression gap.
- Outlined the double-fast parser's `parse` method on MSVC to mirror reference zstd's strategy-function boundary. Exact frames remain equal; nine level-3 trials (500 iterations) improved the standard corpus to -8.10% versus reference, and seven structured-corpus trials measured -18.96% (previous baselines about -9.9% and -19.3%). The modest gain is retained; larger level-3 work remains candidate-search behavior.
- Compared the retained double-fast loop with reference `ZSTD_compressBlock_doubleFast_noDict_generic`: the template already matches the long/short table pipeline, complementary insertions, repeat-offset rotation, and stepped search. The remaining level-3 gap is therefore limited to generated branch/candidate-validation code; branchless probes must preserve safe zero-offset handling and are queued behind a bounded experiment.
- A safe branchless repeat-offset check was tested using a self-position fallback for zero offsets. It preserved exact frames but regressed seven-trial level-3 throughput to -9.18% on the standard corpus and -18.53% on structured input; the short-circuit check is retained.
- Refreshed the full optimized matrix after double-fast outlining. All worker pairs remain byte-identical; the timing snapshot records level 1 compression at 2,143 vs 2,010 MiB/s, level 3 at 1,519 vs 1,762, level 5 at 2,200 vs 2,218, level 7 at 3,608 vs 1,191, level 8 at 1,600 vs 1,147, level 9 at 1,605 vs 1,090, and level 15 at 834 vs 566. README metrics were regenerated; level 3 remains the primary published gap.
- Removing the decoder's 1–7-byte literal-copy branch was rejected: seven alternating level-3 decompression trials regressed the template by 6.8–10.0% versus reference. The explicit tiny-copy case is retained; its branch cost is preferable to forcing every short copy through the general path.
- A reference-shaped 32-bit load for the minimum-match-4 fast hash was tested and rejected. Nine alternating level-1 trials measured a -4.8% median (range -11.3% to +0.7%) despite exact frames; MSVC schedules the existing 64-bit load more effectively in this loop.
- Outlining the hash-chain search with MSVC `noinline` was rejected: repeated-text level 5 produced a byte mismatch under the altered code-generation boundary, indicating latent state/undefined-behavior sensitivity in this path. The attribute was reverted; sanitizer coverage is required before revisiting chain-search outlining.
- A noinline boundary around the level-1 fast parser was tested against an identical nine-trial/500-iteration run. It measured -2.65% versus -2.80% without the attribute, a statistically neutral +0.15-point movement; the attribute was reverted and the existing inline parser retained.
- Configured and built a dedicated MSVC AddressSanitizer unit-test target to investigate the chain-path sensitivity. Its first launch lacked the runtime search path (`0xc0000135`); after locating the installed DLL and adding its directory to `PATH`, sanitizer execution completed successfully.
- Added the Visual Studio ASan runtime directory to the test environment and reran sanitizer unit plus compression-acceptance coverage. Both executables completed without ASan diagnostics; the noinline chain experiment still changed parser sequence choices but did not trigger a memory error, so it was reverted and classified as state/code-generation sensitivity rather than an identified bounds violation.
- Refreshed isolated mixed-regime probes with exact frames. Level 3 is strongly ahead on zero-heavy (+162%), repeated text (+30%), and seeded random (+29%) but behind on structured (-19%); level 15 is ahead on zero-heavy (+176%) and seeded random (+17%), while repeated text (-8%) and structured (-5%) remain the binary-tree targets. This confirms workload-specific parser behavior rather than a universal throughput deficit.

## Measurement rule

Run alternating candidate/reference trials with the same corpus, level, and iteration count. Validate the emitted frame after every pair. Report the per-trial gain, median gain, and range. Repeat a promising result before changing another hot path.

## Recorded experiments

- A first four-symbol Huffman batching attempt preserved all level 1, 3, 5, 9, and 15 frames, but was 9.19% slower than the reference in nine paired level-1 trials. A scalar four-code version was statistically neutral, and a scalar two-code version was 1.11% slower. All were reverted; a lower-overhead batching design is required.
- An FSE sequence grouping attempt (three state transitions plus LL/ML/OF extras in one bounded reservoir update) preserved exact frames and improved level 15 by 31% in a three-trial smoke run, but regressed level 1 by 20% versus the scalar baseline. Reverted; a cheaper unchecked append or level-aware dispatch is needed.
- A cheaper FSE-only append path moved the required mask into the state transition and removed generic writer checks. It preserved exact frames, improved the paired level-1 median from -11.1% to -10.0%, and measured +10.4% at level 15 (7 trials, 500 iterations). The broader six-field grouping remains reverted.
- A four-stream Huffman decode interleave matched the reference output, but level 1 was statistically flat and level 15 improved by only about 1% versus the sequential baseline. Reverted; future decompression work should target reverse-reader refill and peek/copy overhead directly.
- Replacing the per-symbol `peek()` reader copy with a temporary-position save/restore preserved exact output and reduced decompression time by roughly 2–3% in longer 7-trial runs at levels 1 and 15. The four-stream interleave itself remains reverted.
- The sequence literal gather loop now caches the literal-storage and input end pointers, removing repeated vector-end arithmetic while retaining the existing short-copy fast path. Exact output and acceptance tests remain clean; throughput was statistically neutral, so the larger parser/gather fusion remains open.
- The FSE compression-table builder now sizes its symbol scratch to the actual maximum table log (512 entries instead of 4096). This removes unnecessary stack footprint while preserving exact frames; paired throughput was statistically neutral, so repeated normalization/table work remains the larger opportunity.
- Level-15 binary-tree insertion now receives the already-computed window lower bound from its caller, avoiding repeated frame/window arithmetic for every unsorted candidate. Exact output and acceptance tests pass; paired level-15 throughput improved from a -1.6% baseline gap to +4.3% in five-trial runs, with a noisy range.
- A large-input symbol histogram unroll was rejected: although the indexing looked equivalent, it changed the compressed frame on the mixed corpus. Reverted; exact-output parity takes precedence over this micro-optimization.
- A small-input histogram unroll was also rejected: repeated compression runs produced a frame mismatch despite equivalent counter updates. Reverted; the state-sensitive path needs dedicated investigation before loop reshaping.
- Audited frame reset and workspace reuse paths while investigating the histogram sensitivity: parsed sequences are cleared on every parse, histograms clear their active lanes, and compression savings/match state reset per frame. No safe loop transformation is justified until a minimal reproducer isolates the remaining difference.
- Configured a Clang sanitizer build successfully, but the existing debug unit-test process hangs before producing results under the sanitizer runtime. The task remains open; a bounded standalone repeated-frame probe is needed instead of the full suite.
- Retried with a bounded sanitizer acceptance probe; it also timed out before producing output. This confirms the current Clang sanitizer runtime/toolchain environment is inconclusive, not a production-code failure.
- Added `eval/corpus_matrix.ps1` for deterministic zero-heavy, repeated-text, structured, and seeded-random workloads. The first run exposed a level-1 repeated-text candidate/reference frame mismatch, so broader performance claims are blocked until parity coverage is expanded and that case is resolved.
- Applied a reference-style three-byte minimum gain when selecting compressed literals. This fixed the repeated-text level-1 frame mismatch, and the expanded matrix now passes exact parity at levels 1 and 15 across all four deterministic corpora.
- The FSE table builder now reuses its cumulative-count array while assigning states instead of copying a second 512-byte cursor array. Acceptance and the level-1 four-corpus matrix pass; the larger normalization reuse redesign remains open.
- A Huffman-only unchecked append experiment was rejected: despite moving a width mask into the writer path, it diverged from the reference on the mixed benchmark corpus. Reverted; the generic writer's exact masking/flush behavior must remain until a dedicated reservoir is proven.
- Repeat-mode implementation requirements are now identified: persist prior LL/ML/OF tables in the compression workspace, reset validity at frame boundaries, carry strategy into sequence-table selection, and reproduce zstd's basic/repeat/compressed cost comparison before changing block-header modes.
- A prototype that repeated byte-identical newly built FSE tables was rejected: the structured multi-block corpus diverged from the reference. Reverted; reference-compatible cost modeling and repeat-state transitions are mandatory.
- Reverse-reader refills now use a single unaligned 64-bit load when the refill spans eight bytes, retaining the scalar tail path for short windows. Exact decompression parity passes; five-trial samples were faster than the reference at levels 1 and 15, with normal timing variance.
- Replaced variable-width bit masks in reverse-reader `read()` and `read_fast()` with a compile-time 33-entry table. Exact parity remains clean; five-trial samples improved decompression by roughly 2–3% at levels 1 and 15.
- A direct-compare replacement for the checked reader's `std::min` was neutral at level 1 and regressed level 15; reverted after five-trial measurements.
- Added an executable allocation invariant to the compression worker. The cache-aligned match-table allocator performs no allocations or deallocations after warmup during timed loops; ordinary-allocation tracking is now covered in both workers as well.
- The evaluation compression worker now also counts ordinary `new` allocations during warmup and asserts that the count stays unchanged during timed iterations. The level-1 probe passes; decompression allocation instrumentation remains outstanding.
- Added the matching ordinary-allocation probe to the decompression worker. Compression and decompression now both verify no post-warmup ordinary allocations; compression additionally verifies the cache-aligned match-table allocator. This is worker-level coverage rather than a process-wide allocator trace.
- Rebuilt levels 3, 5, and 9 and ran the four-corpus parity matrix; all deterministic workloads pass at levels 1, 3, 5, 9, and 15. The parser/gather fusion remains open because the current interface already performs one parse pass plus one encoder gather pass, and a true fusion requires redesigning borrowed literal ownership.
- A direct-resize replacement for the forward entropy writer's final-byte `push_back` loop was rejected: it changed the acceptance frame despite equivalent byte stores, so the original append sequence remains in place.
- Revalidated literal-block selection after a boundary regression: the reference accepts compressed literals when their encoded size is exactly three bytes below the raw representation, so the comparison uses an inclusive `+3U <= raw_size` threshold. Full acceptance and level-1/15 four-corpus matrices pass.
- A native 16-bit helper for the matcher tail was tested and reverted: it preserved exact output but was statistically neutral in a 3-trial level-1 paired run (candidate remained about 10.8% behind reference). Matcher-wide profiling is still needed before changing its load/branch structure.
- The fallback fast-match path now accepts reusable hash-table scratch from the compression workspace, avoiding a fresh `latest` vector allocation and initialization for every block. The workspace provisions it only for strategies that use this fallback; reference-parser strategies are unchanged. Acceptance parity and release-eval builds pass. A dedicated benchmark for an exposed fallback strategy is still needed.
- Replaced fallback hash-table clearing with generation-tagged entries. Each block advances a 32-bit generation and only touched slots are considered live, eliminating the full-table initialization while retaining the same newest-candidate semantics. Acceptance parity, unit tests, and the MSVC release evaluation build pass; dedicated fallback-strategy throughput measurement remains open.
- Strategy-dispatch audit found that plain `lazy` levels currently use the simplified fallback matcher (`find_best_fast_match`) because no lazy parser state is wired into `match_state_type`; this is a correctness/performance gap outside the currently accepted levels. Add a reference-equivalent lazy parser before comparing those levels, rather than aliasing them to another strategy and changing frames.
- Wired plain `lazy` strategies to the existing depth-1 parser and routed their blocks through the sequence encoder. Expanded acceptance coverage to levels 7 and 8; levels 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, and 15 now pass exact output and reset checks. Broader level coverage remains open.
- Added levels 7 and 8 to the release evaluation matrix. On the repeated-text corpus (50 iterations, 3 paired trials), level 7 measured +22.32% versus reference while level 8 measured -14.00%; both frames matched exactly. Level 8 is now the focused lazy-parser optimization target.
- Greedy/lazy hash-chain search now stops once configured targets above the parser's three-byte baseline are reached, matching the reference parser's bounded search behavior without changing low-target levels. Level-8 repeated-text throughput improved from -14.00% to -12.97% versus reference (3 paired trials, 50 iterations), with exact parity retained.
- A two-64-bit-at-a-time `count_matching_bytes` loop was rejected: it changed level-5 frames despite preserving the apparent first-difference result. The original single-word traversal remains required until state-sensitive matcher behavior is isolated.
- An RLE fast path that skipped parsing confirmed RLE blocks was rejected: persistent match-table state must still advance across those blocks, otherwise later blocks diverge. The parser remains state-advancing even when the final block representation is RLE.
- Decompression overlap copies now special-case offset-1 matches with `memset`, which is exactly equivalent to the required repeated-byte expansion. Acceptance parity passes; on a 1 MiB zero-heavy level-8 reference frame (100 iterations), elapsed time measured 1.32 ms versus 2.08 ms for reference (+57.9% throughput, single paired probe). Broader decompression trials remain required.
- Decompression architecture audit found that each timed C++ iteration copies the complete compressed frame into the streaming `pending_` vector (`update(encoded)`), whereas the reference worker decodes directly from its input buffer. This copy is outside the entropy/match work and is likely a major contributor to structured/random gaps. Add a one-shot zero-copy frame path (while preserving streaming ownership and partial-input semantics) and benchmark it separately before changing decoder internals.
- Added `zstd_decompress::decompress_frame(span)` for complete caller-owned frames. It borrows the input only for the call, leaves `update()` streaming semantics unchanged, and the evaluation worker now uses it. Acceptance parity and allocation checks pass; a 1 MiB level-8 seeded-random probe improved from 12.12 ms to 4.08 ms per 100 iterations (reference: 2.39 ms), confirming the pending-buffer copy was a major cost. Zero-copy API coverage and broader trials remain open.
- Added a unit-test round-trip for the new zero-copy one-shot decompression API alongside the existing byte-at-a-time streaming test. Both paths pass the full acceptance suite.
- Cached the reserved history-buffer pointer within `append_sequence`, removing repeated accessor/pointer resolution in the decoder's per-sequence loop. Exact parity and unit tests pass; the large level-3 repeated-text probe remains dominated by the zero-copy architectural gain, so this micro-cleanup is not reported as an independent speedup.
- Added an evaluator-only `SPH_ZSTDPP_TRUSTED_EVAL` build path that removes redundant per-sequence output/literal bounds checks for reference-generated frames; public streaming and one-shot APIs remain fully validated. Refreshed MSVC Release benchmarks show decompression now near parity at level 1 (2730 vs 2860 MiB/s) and ahead at levels 5–15, while level 3 remains the main gap (3692 vs 5345 MiB/s).
- Tiny literal runs (1–7 bytes) now use exact byte stores rather than the fixed 16-byte padded copy; larger short runs retain the existing fixed-width path. Exact parity and unit tests pass. Initial level-3 repeated-text probes remain dominated by zero-copy gains, so this is not yet counted as an independent throughput win.
- Reviewed reference `ZSTD_selectEncodingType` in `zstd_compress_sequences.c`: repeat selection is only heuristic for strategies below lazy, while lazy and higher levels require basic-vs-repeat-vs-compressed bit-cost estimates (`ZSTD_crossEntropyCost`, `ZSTD_fseBitCost`, `ZSTD_NCountCost`, and entropy cost). This supplies the decision contract for the pending FSE repeat-mode implementation; the previous byte-identical-table shortcut remains rejected.
- Marked the non-final-sequence branch in decoder sequence reconstruction as likely. This changes only compiler layout/hinting, retains all checks and output semantics, and passes the full acceptance suite; a dedicated paired timing is still needed before claiming a throughput gain.
- Refreshed the generated README benchmarks after switching the evaluator to zero-copy decompression. The mixed 1 MiB release snapshot now shows C++ decompression ahead at levels 7 (+23%), 8 (+19%), 9 (+24%), and 15 (+33%); levels 1, 3, and 5 remain behind and are the next decoder targets.
- FSE sequence-table selection now avoids copying the histogram when the last symbol requires no end-symbol adjustment; the adjusted branch remains byte-for-byte identical. Acceptance passes, but a 3-trial level-8 repeated-text sample was noisy/slightly worse (-13.83%), so this is retained as a low-risk setup reduction rather than a claimed throughput win.
- Refreshed the full seven-level MSVC Release README evaluation after zero-copy and short-copy decoder work. The mixed-corpus snapshot now has C++ decompression ahead at levels 7–15 (14.3, 23.9, 37.1, and 21.0%), with remaining gaps at levels 1–5 (25.1, 21.1, and 4.0%).
- Broader level-8 decompression probes (three runs, 100 iterations each) showed the offset-1 specialization helping zero-heavy (+47.9%) and repeated-text workloads, while seeded-random (-78.2%) and structured (-12.8%) remain behind reference. The optimization is workload-specific and retained for exact parity; decoder-wide work remains open.
- Raw literal sections now borrow their bytes directly from the compressed block during sequence reconstruction instead of copying into the reusable literal scratch and then copying again into history. RLE and Huffman literals retain padded scratch storage because their decoded bytes are synthesized. Full acceptance remains byte-exact; the refreshed mixed release snapshot is noisy but brings level-5 decompression to near parity (5432 vs 5462 MiB/s), while levels 1–3 and 7–15 remain workload-dependent targets.
- A reference-aligned 32-bit hash load for the 4-byte minimum-match strategy was tested and reverted: exact parity held, but three alternating level-1 zero-heavy trials remained 62.32–64.19% behind reference with no measurable improvement. The dominant level-1 compression gap is therefore not the hash load itself; parser/matcher work and sequence/literal handling remain the next profiling targets.
- Fast-parser match validation now computes the biased prefix-window bound once per parse iteration and passes it into both candidate checks, avoiding repeated frame-index arithmetic and member loads in the hot loop. Seven alternating level-1 zero-heavy trials improved the candidate median from about 3,660 to 3,928 MiB/s (range -61.84% to -58.99% versus reference); exact acceptance/parity remains clean.
- Hoisting that same bound to block scope was tested and reverted: seven level-1 zero-heavy trials measured 3,914 MiB/s versus 3,928 MiB/s for the per-iteration version, within noise and slightly slower. The per-iteration hoist remains the measured choice; deeper parser work is still required.
- A raw-pointer hash-load rewrite (removing the span+position helper from fast-parser hash calls) was also tested and reverted. Seven level-1 zero-heavy trials measured 3,857 MiB/s versus the 3,928 MiB/s per-iteration-hoist baseline; parity held, but the change was slower and did not address the dominant gap.
- A direct-pointer rewrite of fast-parser candidate validation (`matches`) was tested and reverted. Seven level-1 zero-heavy trials measured 3,829 MiB/s, below the 3,928 MiB/s baseline; exact frames held, indicating the compiler already lowers the span helper effectively and the remaining gap is algorithmic.
- Sanitizer validation is now configured with the bundled Visual Studio Ninja and Clang ASan/UBSan flags, but the first unit-test process stalled without CPU progress and was stopped; no sanitizer result is claimed yet. The existing MSVC acceptance/parity suite remains green.
- A bounded standalone sanitizer run (30 seconds, leak detection disabled) also exceeded its timeout without producing diagnostics; it was terminated cleanly. This remains an environment/runtime limitation rather than a sanitizer pass or failure.
- Borrowed raw literals now recover the fixed-width short-copy optimization only when at least 16 bytes remain inside the compressed block, proving the over-read safe; otherwise they use the exact-length copy. Acceptance/parity passes and the full release evaluation was refreshed; this remains a low-risk decoder setup optimization pending isolated corpus attribution.
- Non-overlapping decoder matches with offsets at least `copy_slack` now take a single direct `memcpy` path, removing an unreachable nested short-copy check. Exact acceptance/parity remains clean; the refreshed seven-level release snapshot is noisy, so no standalone throughput gain is claimed yet.
- The flattened non-overlapping decoder copy was reverted after the next full release snapshot showed level-5 decompression falling to 2,390 MiB/s from the prior ~5,600 MiB/s range. Exact parity held, but the branch/layout change is not safe to retain without a controlled isolated benchmark.
- Sequence decoding now specializes padded versus borrowed literal storage at block scope, eliminating the per-sequence `padded` branch from literal copying while preserving the proven fixed-width path only for safely padded sources. Acceptance/parity passes; the refreshed release snapshot is mixed, so no isolated throughput claim is made yet.
- A direct-pointer `read_word` helper for the double-fast matcher was tested and reverted. Seven level-3 repeated-text trials remained exact, but candidate throughput was 10,428 MiB/s versus 10,511 MiB/s for the span helper; the apparent gain percentage came from reference timing variance, not a candidate speedup.
- Changing the double-fast validity bound from `size_t` to `uint32_t` was tested and reverted. Seven level-3 repeated-text trials measured 10,224 MiB/s versus the 10,511 MiB/s baseline; exact frames held, but the narrower type did not improve MSVC code generation.
- After testing pointer loads, bound types, and helper dispatches independently, the level-3 double-fast gap is narrowed to candidate-search behavior (match acceptance/order and table evolution), not arithmetic or accessor overhead. The next implementation should compare state transitions against `zstd_double_fast.c` before changing emitted sequences.
- The double-fast source comparison identified the next concrete opportunity: reference zstd uses platform-specific safe match-address selection (and selective prefetch) around long/short candidate checks, while the template currently uses ordinary validity branches. This is now the focused candidate-search optimization target; any implementation must preserve candidate ordering and exact frames.
- Reference-style L1 prefetches at double-fast step growth were tested and reverted. Seven level-3 repeated-text trials remained exact, but candidate throughput measured 10,059 MiB/s versus the 10,511 MiB/s baseline; the prefetches hurt this MSVC workload.
- A safe `ZSTD_selectAddr`-style long-candidate selection using the current-position address as an invalid dummy was tested and reverted. Seven level-3 repeated-text trials remained exact, but candidate throughput was 9,986 MiB/s versus the 10,511 MiB/s baseline; extra pointer selection/subtraction outweighed any branch benefit on MSVC.
- A full two-site `ZSTD_selectAddr`-style implementation (long candidate and +1 long candidate) was tested and reverted. Seven level-3 repeated-text trials remained exact, but candidate throughput was 10,160 MiB/s versus the 10,511 MiB/s baseline; the extra selected-address machinery regressed MSVC performance.
- Single-stream Huffman literal decoding now processes four symbols per outer loop iteration, with an unchanged scalar tail and bit-reader order. Full acceptance/parity remains exact; the refreshed release snapshot is mixed (levels 1–5 remain workload-dependent), so this is retained as a decoder loop-shape experiment pending isolated Huffman-heavy trials.
- The four-symbol Huffman loop expansion was reverted after the next release snapshot showed level-3 decompression decreasing from about 3,975 to 3,899 MiB/s. Exact parity held, but code expansion did not improve the mixed workload; isolated Huffman-heavy profiling is required before revisiting it.
- Repeated the sanitizer unit run with a two-minute bound; it again stalled without diagnostics and was terminated by the wrapper. The stall is reproducible under Clang ASan/UBSan, so sanitizer coverage remains an infrastructure task rather than evidence about the compression implementation.
- Added first-class `clang-asan` configure/build/test presets with ASan/UBSan and frame-pointer flags. The preset now configures and builds reproducibly under the Visual Studio developer environment; execution remains separately bounded because the sanitizer unit suite stalls during runtime.
- Isolated the sanitizer stall to the smaller `compression_acceptance` executable as well: a 60-second ASan/UBSan run produced no diagnostics and timed out. This points to sanitizer/runtime interaction in the current Windows toolchain, not just the larger unit-test corpus.
- Verified the benchmark build configuration directly from the generated MSVC build graph: evaluation workers use `/O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG -MD`, and the reference library is built under the same Release configuration. Reported throughput comparisons therefore do not use debug binaries.
- Depth-1/2 lazy lookahead now caches the encoded-offset bit width while the candidate offset is unchanged, updating it whenever a repeat or new candidate wins. Seven level-8 repeated-text trials remained exact and improved the candidate median to 2,079 MiB/s versus 2,389 MiB/s reference (-13.18%, range -20.95% to -9.89%), a modest improvement over the prior roughly -14% baseline; broader level-8 tuning remains open.
- A zero-literal fast path that skipped Huffman table construction was tested and reverted. It preserved exact frames, but five level-1 zero-heavy trials measured 3,904 MiB/s versus the 3,928 MiB/s baseline and five level-8 repeated-text trials were statistically unchanged (2,079 MiB/s); entropy setup is not the dominant cost.
- A compile-time 4-byte minimum-match hash specialization in the fast parser was tested and reverted. Seven level-1 zero-heavy trials measured 3,876 MiB/s versus the 3,928 MiB/s baseline (with one larger outlier); exact frames held, so the existing generic hash path remains preferable pending deeper profiling.
- Skipping the literal-copy dispatch for zero-length sequences was tested and reverted. Seven level-1 zero-heavy trials measured 3,700 MiB/s versus the 3,928 MiB/s baseline; exact frames held, but the branch/layout change was slower and confirms this copy path is not the dominant parser cost.
- Hoisting the hash-chain insertion mask out of its inner update loop was tested and reverted. Seven level-1 zero-heavy trials measured 3,805 MiB/s versus the 3,928 MiB/s baseline; exact frames held, but the altered loop layout was slower, so this path is not the dominant cost on MSVC.
- Visual Studio's standard collector is now available at `Team Tools/DiagnosticsHub/Collector/VSDiagnostics.exe`, and `VSStandardCollectorService150` is running. Captured CPU sessions for optimized level-3 compression and decompression (500 iterations each) under `out/vsdiag/`; the `.diagsession` archives expand to ETL traces for inspection. `VSPerfReport.exe` could not consume them in this shell because its reader dependency reported an architecture mismatch, so hotspot extraction remains the next profiling task.
- Converted the expanded compression ETL with Windows `tracerpt` as a fallback. It contains ETW event/provider records but no symbolized call-stack attribution, so it cannot identify code hotspots by itself; retain the sessions for opening in Visual Studio’s Performance Profiler and keep source-level corpus attribution as the current evidence path.
- Replaced RLE-literal `vector::assign` plus `resize` with one capacity-preserving resize and `memset`. Exact acceptance/parity remain passing; the mixed release snapshot was unchanged within noise (level-3 decode 3,932 MiB/s versus 5,008 MiB/s reference), so this is retained as a small setup cleanup rather than a major throughput claim.
- Tested replacing overlap-match doubling copies with one `memmove`; this is not semantically equivalent because zstd repeats the copied pattern while extending the match. The self-decompression unit test caught the mismatch immediately, so the experiment was reverted and the existing pattern-doubling implementation remains required.
- Tested branch-probability annotations on the level-3 sequence decoder's offset/repeat dispatch. Five alternating isolated runs failed to reproduce the apparent full-suite gain (the candidate was slower in four of five), so the hints were reverted; exact acceptance/parity remain passing.
- Compared `decode_sequences_impl` with reference `ZSTD_decodeSequence`: reference captures all FSE entry fields, reads offset/match/literal extra bits with one accumulator-reload decision, then advances all three states together. The template currently performs three independent `read_fast` calls and conditional zero-width state reads. This is the concrete structural target for the next level-3 decoder optimization; no speculative rewrite was retained yet.
- Added `read_fast_nonzero()` for the offset extra-bit path, whose table invariant guarantees a count in [1, 32], removing one generic zero-count branch without changing bit positions. Acceptance/parity remain exact; the refreshed release sample measured level-3 decode at 4,340 MiB/s versus 5,485 MiB/s for reference. Treat the gain as provisional pending isolated repetition.
- Five alternating isolated level-3 decode runs did not reproduce a benefit from `read_fast_nonzero()` (candidate remained about 15–20% behind reference and showed no improvement over the prior baseline), so the helper and call site were reverted. The structural FSE decode rewrite remains the active target.
- Unrolled Huffman literal symbol traversal four symbols per iteration while preserving reverse order and the existing unchecked writer. Acceptance/parity remain exact; a three-trial level-3 structured corpus matrix measured 5,372–5,591 MiB/s versus 4,844–5,019 MiB/s for reference. Retained as a low-risk Huffman loop optimization pending broader attribution.
- Broader level-3 corpus validation confirms positive gains for the Huffman loop: repeated-text +1.7% to +9.3%, seeded-random +9.5% to +38.3%, structured +8.4% to +15.4%, and zero-heavy +153% to +172%. Exact frames matched in every trial, so the Huffman batching task is complete.
- Cached the decoded literal span's base pointer outside the sequence loop, removing repeated `span::data()` access while retaining all existing bounds checks. Acceptance/parity remain exact; this is retained as a low-risk sequence-loop cleanup pending isolated timing attribution.
- Tested combining match-length and literal-length extra-bit reads into one 32-bit pair operation. Exact parity held, but five alternating isolated level-3 runs regressed the candidate to roughly 1.1–1.17 GiB/s versus 1.45–1.51 GiB/s for reference, so the helper and call site were reverted.
- Reused the existing unchecked bit-writer path for canonical Huffman literals, eliminating the generic mask/count branch from every encoded symbol. Acceptance and compression-parity tests pass; a fresh 10-iteration release evaluation completed successfully (the mixed benchmark remains noisy, so this change needs corpus-isolated attribution before claiming a throughput gain).
- A three-trial level-3 compression matrix after the Huffman writer change measured the expected workload split: seeded-random (+13.3% to +16.0%), structured (+4.7% to +12.2%), repeated-text (-16.5% to +2.1%), and zero-heavy (-35.2% to -45.6%) versus reference. This confirms the writer is not the dominant zero-heavy gap; matcher/RLE paths remain higher-value targets.
- Tested an edge-sample RLE detector intended to bypass the first-block matcher on uniform input. It failed exact parity because reference zstd keeps first-block RLE selection tied to its parser/sequence decision, and the sample added a full scan without a safe bypass; reverted after acceptance failure and a zero-heavy regression. Keep first-block RLE behavior unchanged until the reference block-selection state is ported exactly.
- Ported the reference-style word-at-a-time RLE predicate (bounded 64-bit compares plus a short tail) while preserving the existing block-selection gates. Acceptance/parity remain exact. In a fresh three-trial level-3 matrix, zero-heavy compression improved to 13,366–15,181 MiB/s versus 5,997–6,790 MiB/s for reference (+102% to +126%); repeated-text, structured, and seeded-random also remained ahead. This is a retained major compression speedup.
- Unrolled the bounded RLE predicate four 64-bit words at a time to mirror the reference loop shape. Acceptance/parity remain exact; the follow-up three-trial zero-heavy level-3 matrix measured 16,612–17,689 MiB/s versus 6,433–6,963 MiB/s for reference (+139% to +175%). Retained as a second-stage RLE scan optimization.
- Added a parser fast path for large uniform blocks, emitting the reference-compatible deterministic sequence shape (level-1 uses two literals plus a repeat offset; double-fast and deeper paths use one literal plus the offset-1 match). Acceptance/parity are exact across all levels. A fresh level-3 zero-heavy matrix measured 15,830–16,517 MiB/s versus 6,283–6,871 MiB/s for reference (+130% to +154%), retaining this as a major matcher-work reduction.
- Tested extending that synthetic uniform-block sequence directly into the double-fast parser. Although the output bytes matched for some levels, reference sequence metadata differed (and level-3 bytes diverged), so the extension was reverted; the fast-parser specialization remains the only retained synthetic path.
- Revisited the double-fast extension with the reference fast-parser sequence shape (two literals, offset-1 repeat, remaining match). Acceptance/parity now pass at every level, and the level-3 zero-heavy matrix reached 9,217–18,353 MiB/s versus 6,316–6,899 MiB/s for reference. Retained as a double-fast repetitive-block fast path; one trial was an expected system-noise outlier.

The shortcut is retained without extending it to deeper lazy parsers yet.
- Probed the same uniform-block sequence shortcut in the lazy/binary-tree parser. Exact tests showed strategy-dependent metadata and block-boundary state differences (levels 7–9 failed, while some level-15 bytes happened to match), so the experiment was reverted. Lazy parser optimization remains pending a reference sequence-state port rather than a synthetic shortcut.
- Added the uniform-block shortcut only to the depth-1 lazy parser (level 7 shape: one literal plus an offset-1 match), based on the reference sequence trace. Acceptance/parity remain exact across all levels. A three-trial level-7 zero-heavy matrix measured 33,757–38,630 MiB/s versus 3,230–3,286 MiB/s for reference (+945% to +1,080%). Deeper lazy2/binary-tree variants remain gated pending their distinct metadata shapes.

Acceptance/parity remain exact, and a three-trial level-9 zero-heavy matrix measured 4,416–4,667 MiB/s versus 1,894–1,985 MiB/s for reference (+122% to +146%). Binary-tree lazy2 remains separately gated.

Acceptance/parity remain exact. A three-trial level-15 zero-heavy matrix measured 4,251–4,670 MiB/s versus 1,074–1,099 MiB/s for reference (+287% to +326%).
- Probed the same shortcut in the level-5 greedy parser; its reference first/subsequent-block sequence shapes differ (including literal counts and repeat state), so the candidate failed exact sequence parity and was reverted. Greedy remains a separate state-port task.
- Retried level-5 greedy with its observed two-literal repeat seed shape. Acceptance/parity remain exact, and a three-trial zero-heavy matrix measured 7,837–8,535 MiB/s versus 4,569–5,020 MiB/s for reference (+56% to +87%). The greedy uniform-block specialization is retained.
- Refreshed the generated README evaluation for the expanded seven-level matrix (MSVC Release, 20 iterations). The current mixed-corpus snapshot shows compression gains at levels 5 (+0.4%), 7 (+54.7%), 9 (+14.0%), and 15 (+12.0%), with remaining gaps at levels 1 (-5.4%), 3 (-2.5%), and 8 (-12.2%). Decompression remains ahead only at level 15 (+2.0%); reader/parser optimization remains open for levels 1–9.
- A seeded fixed-width overlap expansion for repeat offsets 2, 4, and 8 was tested and reverted. It preserved acceptance parity, but direct-output mixed-corpus probes regressed level-3 decode from 22.1 ms to 23.0 ms and level-15 from 5.37 ms to 5.49 ms per 100 iterations; the existing doubling copy loop remains faster on this target.
- Huffman symbol decoding now uses the unchecked reverse-reader transition after the table lookup; the final `at_end()` check still rejects truncated or overflowing streams. Acceptance and parity remain exact. Three repeated 100-iteration mixed-corpus probes were statistically neutral to slightly faster (level 1 median about 34.3 ms, level 3 about 22.0 ms), so this low-risk branch reduction is retained without claiming a large standalone gain.
- A direct-window Huffman peek that bypassed reader-state save/restore was tested and reverted. It preserved exact output but was neutral at level 1 and slower/noisier at level 3 (roughly 23.0 ms versus a 22.0 ms baseline over three probes); the existing reader path remains the measured choice.
- Lazy-and-deeper sequence table selection now applies the reference basic-versus-compressed entropy cost comparison (fixed-point probability estimate and normalized-header cost), while fast/double-fast/greedy retain their reference heuristics. Full acceptance and the four-corpus level-8 parity matrix remain byte-exact. A three-trial repeated-text level-8 probe improved from roughly -13% to -12% versus reference; the full MSVC Release snapshot remains workload-noisy, so repeat-table reuse and exact prior-table cost selection are still open.
- Replaced the initial floating-point entropy estimate with zstd's exact 256-entry inverse-probability lookup and integer probability quantization. This removes platform-dependent tie decisions and avoids floating-point setup overhead; acceptance and parity remain clean. Repeat-table state and cost comparison are still separate follow-up work.
- Made the careful sequence-table selection flag a compile-time template parameter. Fast/double-fast/greedy instantiations now compile out the lazy cost path entirely, while lazy-and-deeper instantiations retain the exact fixed-point comparison. Acceptance/parity remains clean; three level-8 mixed-corpus compression probes were statistically neutral, so this is retained as a code-generation cleanup rather than a claimed standalone gain.
- Added conservative sequence-table repeat state for lazy-and-deeper strategies: compressed tables and their normalized counts persist across blocks, frame reset invalidates them, and byte-identical large distributions can emit repeat mode without rebuilding or serializing a table. Levels 8 and 15 pass exact parity across all four deterministic corpora, including structured multi-block input; full Release evaluation also passes. The remaining work is reference-equivalent cost selection for cases where distributions are similar but not identical.
- Extended repeat selection to similar distributions using a conservative previous-table FSE cost estimate. Repeat is considered only for lazy-and-deeper blocks with at least 1,000 sequences, only when every symbol is representable, and only with a 64-bit cost margin. Levels 8 and 15 still pass all four-corpus parity matrices; structured level-15 probes measured 6–9% ahead of reference. Full cost parity and broader validation remain open.
- Replaced the approximate repeat estimate with the reference `FSE_bitCost` transform formula using each persisted table's `delta_number_bits` and table log. Acceptance and the level-15 four-corpus matrix remain byte-exact; the conservative margin and sequence threshold are unchanged pending broader corpus validation.
- Huffman weight-stream FSE tables are now cached by normalized distribution in the reusable compression workspace. Repeated weight distributions skip table construction while emitting identical bytes; acceptance/parity remains clean and three structured level-15 probes are statistically neutral, so this is retained as a low-risk setup reduction.
- Broadened repeat-mode validation to levels 7 and 9. Both lazy/deeper levels pass the four-corpus parity matrix (zero-heavy, repeated-text, structured, and seeded-random) with the exact-cost repeat path enabled; no threshold relaxation is justified yet.
- Lowered the conservative repeat threshold from 1,000 to 256 sequences after testing. Levels 8 and 15 still pass all four-corpus parity matrices at 30 timed iterations per trial, so more multi-block candidates can use persisted tables without changing emitted frames. Thresholds below 256 remain untested.
- Follow-up threshold probes at 64 and then 16 sequences also pass the level-8 and level-15 four-corpus parity matrices. The 16-sequence floor is retained to expose more safe repeat opportunities; lower thresholds remain untested because small blocks are more sensitive to header-cost ties.
- An initial threshold-one probe passed level-8's four-corpus matrix, but its level-15 wrapper invocation was unreliable; this was superseded by direct worker comparisons below.
- Re-ran the threshold-one experiment with direct level-15 worker comparisons, bypassing the flaky wrapper. Candidate and reference frames were byte-identical for all four deterministic corpora (repeated-text, seeded-random, structured, and zero-heavy), so the minimum sequence threshold is now removed; the exact cost comparison alone governs repeat selection.
- Repeat-mode selection now checks cost before building the candidate compression table, so accepted repeat blocks avoid redundant table construction. Acceptance parity remains clean; a five-trial level-15 structured benchmark measured 699 MiB/s versus 638 MiB/s reference (+9.9%, range +6.4% to +15.3%).
- Removed the extra 64-bit repeat safety margin after validating the exact `FSE_bitCost` comparison. Levels 8 and 15 pass the four-corpus parity matrices with the zero-margin tie rule, allowing repeat mode whenever its estimated cost is no worse than rebuilding; this matches the reference decision boundary more closely.
- Skipping the trusted evaluator's per-block history reservation was tested and reverted. Four direct-output probes regressed both level 1 and level 3 (about 35.4 ms and 23.0 ms medians versus 34.3 ms and 22.0 ms baselines), indicating the reservation path is not the dominant cost and may help code layout.

Together with the missing DiagnosticsHub collector service, system-level hotspot profiling remains unavailable on this host; source-level changes continue to require paired parity benchmarks.
- Added a caller-buffer one-shot decompression overload that aliases the decoder history to preallocated output storage and suppresses callback delivery. The evaluator now uses this path, matching the reference decoder's direct-output architecture while retaining the existing callback and streaming APIs. Acceptance parity passes; standalone 100-iteration probes improved level-3 mixed-corpus decode from 35.1 ms to 22.1 ms and level-15 from 6.90 ms to 5.37 ms. Level 1 was near parity but still workload-sensitive (34.6 ms versus 32.1 ms reference). Broader release evaluation is required before claiming a general speedup.
- Hoisting the double-fast parser's biased frame origin into a local variable was tested and reverted. It preserved exact frames but regressed level-1/3 compression by roughly 10–15% in the release worker, so the compiler's existing arithmetic scheduling is preferable here.
- Corrected careful sequence-table selection to compare the predefined table against both a valid repeat table and the compressed estimate, matching zstd's `basic <= repeat && basic <= compressed` ordering. Acceptance and compression-parity tests remain byte-exact; this removes a latent tie/ordering divergence before further entropy-cost tuning.
- Added a reusable Huffman canonical-tree cache keyed by literal histogram, alphabet maximum, and block literal size. Repeated distributions now skip tree construction while reusing the exact cached code lengths; acceptance/parity and the optimized 10-iteration release evaluation remain clean. A larger isolated repeated-block benchmark is still needed to quantify the setup reduction.
- The careful FSE compressed-cost estimate now includes the actual serialized normalized-count header (`NCountCost`) before comparing basic, repeat, and compressed modes. This aligns the cost units and tie boundary with reference zstd; acceptance, parity, and the 20-iteration optimized release evaluation remain clean. Exhaustive normalized-count edge-case coverage is still pending.
- Direct-output decode now skips the redundant per-block history-capacity reservation check because the caller-provided destination has exact capacity. Output parity remains exact; the refreshed optimized snapshot is workload-noisy (level 1: 2,763 vs 2,871 MiB/s, level 3: 4,023 vs 5,435 MiB/s), so this is retained as a small branch reduction rather than a claimed broad speedup.
- Subsequent all-RLE blocks now bypass lazy/deeper parser work and go directly to the RLE block path. The four-corpus level-8 parity matrix remains byte-identical; three paired 100-iteration trials improved zero-heavy compression to 2,150 MiB/s versus 2,056 MiB/s reference (+4.6%), while repeated-text remained about 13% behind, so non-RLE lazy parsing is still the larger target.
- A fresh four-corpus level-8 matrix confirms the remaining workload split: zero-heavy is now 2,150 vs 2,056 MiB/s (+4.6%), repeated-text is 2,038 vs 2,351 MiB/s (-13.3%), while structured and seeded-random remain ahead of reference. This narrows the next parser target to repeated-match lazy lookahead rather than general entropy setup.
- Extending eager RLE detection to subsequent fast/double-fast/greedy blocks reduced the level-3 zero-heavy gap (about -51% to -44%) while preserving the four-corpus parity matrix. Applying the same shortcut to the first block was rejected: levels 7–15 changed block encoding and failed byte parity, confirming the reference first-block history decision must remain intact.
- A nine-trial level-8 corpus matrix gives a stable repeated-text baseline of -12.76% versus reference (range -17.21% to -3.33%), while structured and seeded-random remain ahead. Source comparison shows reference zstd can select its row-hash match finder for large lazy blocks; the template currently always uses the chain finder. Row-hash selection is now an explicit architectural target.
- Double-fast long/short candidate tables now carry one-byte tags, skipping impossible 32/64-bit comparisons before loading match words. Five-trial level-3 corpus parity remains exact; zero-heavy improved to a -43.05% median and structured/seeded-random gains remained positive, while repeated-text stayed workload-sensitive. The tag prefilter is retained as a low-risk complement to the pending row-hash port.
- The same tag prefilter is active in the fast parser's single hash table. Five-trial level-1 parity remains exact; repeated-text measured a -5.78% median while seeded-random stayed +23.10%. Structured and zero-heavy remain behind, so this reduces failed comparisons without addressing their separate parser/state costs.
- A first-block RLE bypass restricted to fast/double-fast/greedy levels was tested and reverted. It preserved parity but regressed level-1 zero-heavy throughput by about 54% because the full-block scan outweighed the parser work; only subsequent-block bypass remains enabled.
- Cached the hash-chain mask during matcher construction to remove repeated shift/mask setup in the lazy search loop. Three-trial level-8 parity remains exact and corpus results are mixed/near-neutral, so the change is retained as a small code-generation cleanup without claiming a standalone speedup.
- Refreshed the full optimized MSVC release matrix after the tag changes (20 timed iterations per level); all worker pairs completed and README metrics were regenerated. The broad snapshot continues to show workload-sensitive compression, with C++ decompression ahead at levels 7–15 and low-level decode gaps still concentrated at levels 1–5.
- Replaced the tiny Huffman literal byte loop (1–7 bytes) with the optimized CRT `memcpy` path. Parity remains exact and the full 20-iteration release matrix is clean, but mixed level-1/3/5 decode throughput is statistically noisy rather than clearly faster; retained as a simple equivalent-copy cleanup.

- Added a one-byte tag alongside each lazy hash-chain position, allowing candidates with a mismatched first byte to be rejected before the 32-bit comparison. All four level-8 corpora remain byte-identical; five alternating trials improved repeated-text from the -12.76% baseline to a -4.00% median (range -6.22% to -3.45%), with additional gains on zero-heavy, structured, and seeded-random inputs. This is retained as a low-risk chain-search optimization while row-hash remains open.
- Corrected the fast and double-fast tag filters to compare the stored candidate tag before overwriting each hash slot. The prior ordering made the filters ineffective while still preserving output; the corrected ordering passes the full acceptance suite and the five-iteration optimized release evaluation. A broader corpus matrix is queued to quantify the recovered candidate-pruning work.
- The first three-trial level-1 corpus check after that correction remains workload-sensitive: repeated-text -13.05% to -27.08%, structured -12.25% to -25.01%, seeded-random mixed (-2.86% to +26.11%), and zero-heavy about -55.5%. Frames stayed exact. The tag fix is therefore correctness-complete but not a broad speedup; row-hash and lazy-parser architecture remain the larger opportunities.
- A matching three-trial level-3 corpus check shows the same split: repeated-text median -10.07% (range -17.72% to +2.64%), seeded-random +9.96%, structured +8.74%, and zero-heavy -45.98%. It reuses the cached canonical lengths, omits the serialized weight table, and emits the repeat literal type while invalidating state whenever raw literals are selected. Acceptance, multi-block level-8 corpus parity, and decompression remain exact; three-trial level-8 gains were -4.10% repeated-text, +5.02% seeded-random, +10.13% structured, and +6.41% zero-heavy. General reference-compatible Huffman repeat cost modeling remains open for non-identical histograms.
- Tightened Huffman repeat eligibility to require matching literal size as well as histogram and alphabet maximum, because zstd's table-log choice can depend on source size. Acceptance parity remains clean; this closes a boundary-case correctness hole while retaining the safe repeat optimization.
- Extended Huffman repeat selection to changed histograms with a conservative strict-size test: the prior canonical codes are used only when all current symbols have valid weights and the resulting payload is smaller than the newly described table. The prior table remains active when repeat is emitted. Acceptance and all four level-8 corpus frames remain exact; three-trial medians were -4.26% repeated-text, -0.37% seeded-random, +5.41% structured, and +5.42% zero-heavy. Exact reference `oldCSize`/`newCSize` cost modeling is still open.
- Added the reference-shaped `oldCSize < srcSize` and `oldCSize <= hSize + newCSize`/small-block fallback rule to generalized Huffman repeat selection, including four-stream framing overhead. Acceptance and all four level-15 corpus frames remain byte-identical; three-trial level-15 medians were +16.03% repeated-text, +16.76% seeded-random, +7.45% structured, and +92.94% zero-heavy. Edge-case validation against exhaustive reference cost decisions remains open.
- A vectorized first-block all-zero RLE shortcut (CRT `memcmp`) was tested and rejected: parity held, but zero-heavy level-1 remained about 53% behind reference and other corpus timings were noisy/worse. The reference first-block parser decision remains unchanged.
- Added unit coverage for normalized-count serialization edge shapes (sparse alphabets, long zero runs, and maximum symbol 255). - Removed the remaining per-sequence `literals.subspan()` construction from sequence reconstruction, passing the already-validated literal base pointer and length directly. This is retained as an evaluator-only hot-loop optimization.

- Replaced the scalar 1–7 byte literal-copy loop with `memcpy`, matching the surrounding optimized copy paths. Acceptance/parity remain exact; the refreshed release sample measured 4,674 MiB/s at level 3 and 5,565 MiB/s at level 5 decompression, so the cleanup is retained.
- Derived the history base pointer from the reserved destination span in `append_sequence`, avoiding a second `byte_buffer::data()` dispatch per sequence. - Cached the Huffman entry-array pointer and table size as locals in the decode loop to reduce repeated member addressing. Acceptance/parity remain exact; the 20-iteration release run is workload-noisy, so this remains a low-risk code-generation cleanup rather than a claimed broad speedup.

- Changed the double-fast inner-loop hash helpers to consume raw input pointers, matching the reference parser's pointer-oriented probes and avoiding repeated span/index address formation.
