- Cached the binary-tree mask derived from the chain-table size at match-state construction, removing repeated shift/parameter resolution in update, insertion, and search helpers. Acceptance/parity remain exact; seven-trial level-15 repeated-text timing was 1,031 versus 1,230 MiB/s (-15.04%), within the existing baseline range, so this is retained as a neutral code-generation cleanup.
- Passing cached input/table pointers into binary-tree update and candidate-insertion calls was tested and reverted. The seven-trial level-15 repeated-text probe measured 1,038 versus 1,219 MiB/s (-15.22%), no better than the existing baseline; MSVC's current inlining of the span-based helpers is retained.
- Verified the generated MSVC release worker rules directly: candidate and reference evaluation objects both use `/O2`, `/DNDEBUG`, and the explicit `/Ob3` inlining option. The published performance comparisons are therefore optimized-vs-optimized, not debug-vs-release.
- Added an opt-in `SPH_ZSTDPP_TRACE_BT` diagnostic build switch. When enabled for the level-15 candidate worker, it reports unsorted catch-up visits, main-tree visits, and match-length extensions; the default build has no counter code or timing overhead. Reference-side equivalent counters and comparative runs remain pending.
- Verified the trace build compiles and runs: on the repeated-text level-15 corpus (20 iterations), it reported 672 unsorted visits, 168 main-tree visits, and 840 match extensions per timed frame. This gives a concrete baseline for the pending reference-instrumented comparison.
- Instrumented both implementations on the same repeated-text level-15 corpus. The template and reference each perform 672 unsorted visits and 168 main-tree visits per frame, while the template reports 840 match extensions. Traversal counts therefore match exactly; the remaining level-15 compression gap is outside extra binary-tree candidate visits.
- Completed the reference match-extension instrumentation. On the same traced corpus, template and reference both report 672 unsorted visits, 168 main-tree visits, and 840 match extensions per frame. Binary-tree traversal and extension-attempt counts are fully identical; further level-15 work should target per-visit code generation or entropy/block assembly rather than traversal semantics.
- Extended the counter comparison to structured, seeded-random, and zero-heavy level-15 corpora. Structured counts matched (822,696 unsorted / 142,233 main / 964,929 extensions); seeded-random matched (9,933 / 62,643 / 72,576); zero-heavy intentionally diverged because the template's validated RLE shortcut avoids traversal (0 / 0 / 0 versus reference 0 / 1,323 / 1,491). SHA-256 frame hashes matched for all three cases.
- With traversal counts now matching across non-RLE corpora, the next level-15 investigation is generated-code parity for `count_matching_bytes<true>`: compare load/compare scheduling and inlining at its call sites before attempting any further algorithmic change.
- Added and exercised an opt-in phase timer for the level-15 candidate worker. On a 100-iteration repeated-text trace, parser work accounted for 69.1 ms, sequence/entropy encoding 0.52 ms, and output emission 0.03 ms; parser-generated code is decisively the next optimization target.
- Tested replacing binary-tree `count_matching_bytes<true>` calls with the non-separated instantiation (now structurally similar after the first-word loop reshaping). Seven-trial level-15 repeated-text throughput fell to 900 versus 1,268 MiB/s (-29.21%), so the separated-word specialization is retained.
- Unrolled the separated-word match counter by two 64-bit comparisons in its long-match loop, leaving the scalar tail and bounded loads unchanged. Acceptance/parity remain exact; seven-trial level-15 repeated-text timing improved to 1,087 versus 1,255 MiB/s (-13.41%), and five-trial structured timing reached 746 versus 746 MiB/s (+0.45%). The targeted gain justifies retaining the unroll.
- Applied the same two-word unroll to the non-separated counter path used by double-fast. Seven-trial level-3 repeated-text timing measured 12,233 versus 9,597 MiB/s (+27.85%), and five-trial seeded-random timing measured 3,139 versus 2,783 MiB/s (+13.12%); frame bytes remained exact. The unroll is retained for both counter specializations.
- Refreshed the full optimized 20-iteration release matrix after both counter unrolls. All worker pairs remained byte-identical; the snapshot measured level-15 compression at 370 vs 521 MiB/s and level-3 compression at 1,567 vs 1,673 MiB/s (candidate vs reference). README metrics were regenerated.
- Follow-up validation with nine trials and 500 iterations confirms the level-15 repeated-text unroll result is stable at 1,092 vs 1,254 MiB/s (-13.04%, range -15.53% to -11.78%). The isolated full-matrix “370 vs 521” snapshot was timing noise, not a sustained template lead.
- Matched the reference hasher's access width for compile-time minimum-match-4 strategies: the template now loads one 32-bit word instead of an unnecessary 64-bit word before the 32-bit multiplicative hash. Acceptance and compression parity remain exact; the refreshed optimized 20-iteration matrix is clean and measures level-15 compression at 404 vs 338 MiB/s, level 7 at 3,532 vs 1,301 MiB/s, and level 5 at 2,130 vs 1,730 MiB/s (candidate vs reference). Corpus-specific validation remains necessary because the matrix is timing-sensitive.
- Applied the same access-width correction to double-fast's short hash: minimum-match-4 now uses a 32-bit load while 5/6/7 retain the required 64-bit hash input. Acceptance and compression parity remain exact; a second optimized 20-iteration matrix measured level-15 compression at 620 vs 489 MiB/s, level 9 at 1,739 vs 1,113 MiB/s, and level 5 at 2,140 vs 2,107 MiB/s (candidate vs reference). The improvement is retained; broader corpus trials remain queued.
- A five-trial, 200-iteration level-15 corpus matrix after both hash-width fixes confirms the remaining repeated-text gap is stable (candidate 1,057–1,090 vs reference 1,238–1,276 MiB/s, roughly -13% to -17%), while structured is +1–10% and zero-heavy is +172–176%. Seeded-random is too scheduler-sensitive at this run length. This keeps row-hash/large-repeated-text behavior as the next architectural target rather than further generic hashing tweaks.
- A MSVC-only native-unaligned-load replacement for the portable `memcpy` match/hash helpers was tested and reverted. Acceptance and frame parity remained exact, but seven level-15 repeated-text trials stayed around -13% to -15% versus reference (one scheduler outlier reached -24%), showing no repeatable gain from changing the load spelling; portable loads are retained.
- Cached the careful FSE selector's compressed and repeat costs so each candidate distribution computes them once instead of twice, without changing the exact tie rules. Acceptance and the optimized 20-iteration matrix remain byte-exact; the matrix is timing-sensitive but measures level-15 compression at 750 vs 551 MiB/s and level 7 at 2,579 vs 1,611 MiB/s (candidate vs reference). Retain as a setup-cost reduction pending longer multi-block trials.
- A longer nine-trial, 500-iteration level-8 paired run on the parity-safe corpus measures 1,653.84 vs 1,399.13 MiB/s (median, +19.50%; gain range +2.69% to +34.63%) with exact frame bytes. This supports retaining the FSE cost-cache change, while the phase-reset row-hash parity case remains excluded from performance claims.
- Row-match storage now uses cache-aligned allocation for both hash words and tag bytes, matching the reference's aligned row layout while retaining one-time construction allocation. A real Release rebuild and the full acceptance suite pass; the matcher remains unwired until its salted cache transitions and candidate order are proven byte-exact.
- Extended row-table unit coverage to assert 64-byte alignment for both arrays and zero allocations across reset, insertion, and candidate enumeration. The rebuilt Release acceptance suite passes; this is now a hard gate for the eventual parser integration.
- Added an allocation-free eight-entry rolling row-hash cache matching `ZSTD_row_fillHashCache`/`ZSTD_row_nextCachedHash` slot replacement semantics, with independent fill, rollover, and ordering tests. Acceptance and compression parity remain exact; parser wiring is still gated on reproducing the reference salt transition and candidate ordering.
- Switched active fast, double-fast, and greedy matcher tag arrays to cache-aligned storage, removing an alignment mismatch with their hash tables. Acceptance/parity remain exact; a five-trial, 500-iteration level-3 compression probe measured 1,534 vs 1,722 MiB/s (candidate vs reference), within the existing baseline range, so the low-risk layout change is retained.
- Measurement-only full release evaluation after tag alignment remained byte-exact. The 20-iteration mixed snapshot measured compression at 2,078/2,061 (level 1), 1,447/1,591 (level 3), 1,987/1,992 (level 5), 3,580/1,794 (level 7), 1,593/1,046 (level 8), 1,605/1,009 (level 9), and 481/344 MiB/s (level 15), candidate/reference. Results are consistent with existing workload-sensitive baselines; the layout change is retained without claiming a broad speedup.
- A longer nine-trial, 500-iteration level-3 paired run after tag alignment remained exact and measured 1,538.5 vs 1,718.57 MiB/s (median, -10.28%; gain range -13.89% to +0.36%). This is within the prior level-3 range and provides no basis for reverting the alignment change.
- Corrected the rolling row-hash cache fill helper to use the reference's inclusive end-pointer contract, and added a short-range regression test covering the final position. The rebuilt Release acceptance suite remains fully green.
- Reference-source audit pinpoints the remaining salt invariant for row integration: on a context reset, `hashSalt` is advanced from the prior block's accumulated `hashSaltEntropy` before the reusable tag table is considered; each row search then adds its selected hash to that entropy. The next prototype must preserve this ordering across phase-reset blocks.
- Added an allocation-free `row_hash_salt_state` helper implementing the reference transition: cumulative 32-bit entropy, normal-reset salt advancement, and dictionary-reset salt clearing. Independent transition tests pass along with the full Release acceptance suite; this removes another source of ambiguity from the gated parser integration.
- Made the row-cache inclusive fill count overflow-safe at the 32-bit index boundary; normal fills are unchanged. Release unit and compression-parity tests remain green.
- Added a single salted row-hash dispatcher for minimum-match formulas 4 through 8, with direct unit coverage. This centralizes the reference hash selection for the upcoming parser hot loop; Release acceptance and parity remain exact.
- Extended row-table candidate-order tests to 32- and 64-entry rows, verifying newest-first circular traversal beyond the original 16-entry case. Release unit and compression-parity tests remain green.
- Composed the tested row table, rolling hash cache, and salt state into an allocation-free `row_match_state` seam with update/search/reset operations. It is not enabled in production parsing yet; a direct unit test verifies update-to-search flow, and the full Release acceptance suite passes.
- Corrected `row_match_state::update` to consume the rolling cache through `next()` at every position, replacing each returned slot with the hash eight positions ahead as the reference does. Release unit and compression-parity tests remain green.
- Extended row-state coverage beyond the eight-entry cache window, verifying rollover and the reference-equivalent 8-prefill plus one replacement hash per updated position. Release acceptance remains green.
- Added workspace caching for derived Huffman repeat-table canonical codes, invalidated when the repeat tree changes. Release frames remain exact; a measurement-only 20-iteration matrix was mixed (level-5 compression 1,808 vs 2,112 MiB/s, level-15 492 vs 403), so the optimization is retained pending isolated repeat-Huffman corpus trials rather than claimed as a broad gain.
- Isolated repeated-text validation now supports retaining the Huffman code cache: nine alternating level-5 trials (500 iterations) measured 7,152 vs 6,562 MiB/s (median, +8.60%; range +6.96% to +11.04%) with exact frames. Level 8 remained -14.27% (2,180 vs 2,530 MiB/s), confirming its gap is dominated by the pending row matcher rather than this setup cache.
- A contrasting structured level-5 corpus also improved with the cache: nine alternating trials (500 iterations) measured 4,066.63 vs 3,078.21 MiB/s (median, +30.92%; range +13.52% to +43.34%) with exact frames. This supports retaining the repeat-code cache as a real setup optimization.
- Low-redundancy seeded-random level-5 validation remained positive: nine alternating trials (500 iterations) measured 2,305.63 vs 1,735.76 MiB/s (median, +34.08%; range +13.23% to +43.41%) with exact frames. The repeat-code cache is retained across all tested corpus regimes.
- Refreshed the published README benchmark table after the repeat-code cache change using the optimized 20-iteration evaluator; all seven compression/decompression pairs remained byte-identical.
- Eliminated the cached repeat-code reconstruction loop by storing fully derived `huffman_code` entries in the workspace. Acceptance/parity remain exact; a fresh nine-trial repeated-text level-5 probe measured 7,256.24 vs 6,704.01 MiB/s (median, +8.81%; range +6.44% to +13.04%), modestly above the prior cache result.
- Level-15 repeated-text isolation remains parser-bound after the cache: seven alternating trials (300 iterations) measured 1,093.06 vs 1,238 MiB/s (median, -12.30%; range -14.24% to -7.13%), with exact frames. This confirms the Huffman optimization does not explain the remaining high-level gap.
- Corrected the composed row state's search operation to accumulate each selected hash into `hashSaltEntropy`, matching the reference before the next reset; added a regression assertion that the salt itself changes only on reset. Release acceptance remains green.
- Rechecked host profiling availability: `VSDiagnostics.exe` is installed and responds to help, but `VSStandardCollectorService150` and `diagsvc` remain stopped; WPA exporter also cannot initialize because the host denies its profile directory. Symbolized trace analysis remains an environment blocker, not a code-validation substitute.
- Replaced per-sequence FSE entry copies with references as a decoder experiment. A seven-trial, 500-iteration level-3 probe was workload/scheduler-sensitive (candidate ranged from 3% faster to 18% slower) and had a slower median, so the change was reverted; the existing copies are retained pending generated-code evidence.
- Tested MSVC whole-program optimization (`/GL` + `/LTCG`) as a possible way to recover template hot-loop code generation. The IPO build remained frame-exact but severely regressed the header-only workers (level 3: 207 vs 1,808 MiB/s; level 15: 80 vs 344 MiB/s in five-trial probes), while reference throughput stayed near baseline. IPO is therefore rejected for this codebase; future gains must come from targeted source/layout changes rather than global link-time optimization.
- Removed the MSVC `noinline` barrier from the binary-tree match search. Level-15 tracing had already shown identical reference/template traversal counts, so the barrier only added a call boundary to the parser hot loop. A seven-trial, 300-iteration repeated-text probe remained byte-exact and improved the template to 479.16 vs 374.83 MiB/s (median, +13.22%; gain range +7.24% to +68.20%). This is a confirmed level-15 parser code-generation win; the analogous double-fast wrapper remains a separate experiment.
- Removed the remaining MSVC `noinline` barrier from the double-fast parser as a follow-up. A seven-trial level-3 repeated-text probe stayed exact at 1,523.38 vs 1,685.41 MiB/s (median, -9.99%; range -12.51% to -1.51%), essentially the established baseline. The barrier is not useful for this parser either, and the source now leaves both hot parser entry points available for normal optimization.
- Narrowed the hot parser `match_result` length/offset fields from `size_t` to `uint32_t`, matching zstd's block/index bounds and reducing state width without changing the serialized representation. Release acceptance/parity remain green. Short paired probes were effectively neutral on the mixed corpus (level 3: -2.80% median; level 15: +0.60%), so this is retained as a low-risk register-pressure cleanup while stronger corpus-specific evidence is gathered.
- Prototyped production row-hash dispatch for non-binary-tree strategies using the allocation-free row-state seam. Frames stayed exact on the mixed corpus, but the standalone state duplicated the existing hash/chain tables and was catastrophically slower (level 5: 189 vs 1,625 MiB/s, median over three trials). Reverted the prototype; the next row implementation must replace/fuse the existing tables and update loop, not add a parallel matcher.
- A second fused row experiment reused the existing hash table/tag allocation (no duplicate row storage), but still collapsed to ~91% behind reference at level 5 (191 vs 2,128 MiB/s) while retaining exact frames. The bottleneck is now identified as scalar per-position row update/hash work versus the reference's SIMD tag-mask and cache path; a production row implementation needs vectorized tag matching and a fused update/search loop, not just shared storage.
- Ported the reference row matcher’s SIMD tag-mask primitive into `row_match_table::collect_candidates`, using SSE2 comparisons with a portable scalar fallback. Existing 16/32/64-entry candidate-order and allocation tests plus full Release acceptance/parity pass. This removes scalar tag scanning from the reusable row primitive; parser integration remains gated until the surrounding update loop is fused with the same vectorized path.
- Replaced row-table candidate enumeration’s full slot scan with a rotated SIMD match mask and trailing-zero bit scan, matching reference circular order while skipping nonmatching tags entirely. All 16/32/64-entry ordering and low-limit tests plus Release acceptance/parity pass; this completes the reusable row primitive’s vectorized selection path. End-to-end parser speed remains pending fused integration.
- Added `row_hash_fixed<MinimumMatch>` compile-time dispatch for the four through eight-byte row hash formulas. This matches reference row-search instantiation and removes the runtime minimum-match switch from the future fused hot loop. Unit coverage verifies the specialized formulas; Release acceptance/parity remain green.
- Added compile-time row-log specializations for row-table insertion and candidate collection. Runtime callers retain clamped dispatch, while the hot implementation uses fixed row widths and no per-entry `countr_zero`/shift derivation. Release acceptance/parity remain green; this is groundwork for the fused parser path rather than an end-to-end benchmark claim.
- Retried a fresh VSDiagnostics CPU session after the collector service was reported running. The executable now reaches `CreateSession` but fails with “Value does not fall within the expected range” before launching the worker; no new profile was produced. Host-side profiling remains unavailable, so source-level paired measurements remain the authoritative optimization gate.
- Measured the hash-chain byte-tag filter against a no-tag control. Removing the filter preserved exact frames but worsened a seven-trial level-3 mixed-corpus probe to 1,300.95 vs 1,704.73 MiB/s (-22.90%), confirming the extra tag load is strongly repaid by avoided match probes. The tag side table is retained; further chain work should focus on its layout/prefetch rather than removal.
- Tested selective prefetching of the next hash-chain tag/link after each candidate. Exact frames held, but seven-trial level-3 throughput remained at the baseline (1,567.84 vs 1,747.88 MiB/s, -10.30%; range -13.39% to +5.52%), so the extra prefetch instructions were reverted.
- Switched SIMD row-tag loads from `_mm_loadu_si128` to `_mm_load_si128`. The cache-aligned allocator and 16/32/64-byte row geometry guarantee alignment for every chunk; MSVC and Clang Release builds plus full acceptance/parity pass. This removes the unaligned-load path from the reusable row primitive.
- Tested marking the hash-chain tag/probe success branch `[[unlikely]]`. Exact frames held, but a seven-trial level-3 probe measured 1,569.07 vs 1,713.72 MiB/s (-11.15%), with no improvement over the existing layout; the annotation was reverted.
- Added fixed-minimum-match `row_hash_cache::fill_fixed` and `next_fixed` paths that call the compile-time hash formulas directly, avoiding generic hasher dispatch in the future fused parser. Unit coverage verifies fill/rollover equivalence; Release acceptance/parity remain green.
- Composed the fixed hash-cache, row-log table, and salt state into allocation-free `row_match_state::update_fixed`/`search_fixed` APIs, with unit coverage for rollover, salt preservation, and candidate collection. Release acceptance/parity remain green. These APIs are integration groundwork only; the production parser still needs a fused row update/search path to avoid duplicating its existing match finder.
- Reference audit clarifies the fused-call invariant: `ZSTD_row_update_internal()` inserts positions strictly before the current input pointer; `ZSTD_RowFindBestMatch()` then obtains the current hash, enumerates candidates, and inserts the current position only after candidate collection. The production port must preserve this update/search/insert ordering (including lazy-skipping behavior) rather than calling the current inclusive helper around the search.
- Added allocation-free `row_match_state::find_fixed`, a tested fused seam that enforces the reference update-before-search/insert-after-search ordering and advances `next_to_update` exactly once. It is intentionally not wired into the production parser yet; lazy-skipping and candidate scoring still need to be mapped before enabling it.
- Reference row lazy-skipping constants are now pinned for the integration test: skip only when the current pointer is more than 384 positions ahead, retain the first 96 update positions, resume at 32 positions before the current pointer, and search with the current position inserted afterward. These bounds match `ZSTD_row_update_internal()` and must be applied to the existing frame-index bias without changing parser tie-breaking.
- Reran the optimized MSVC Release matrix after the row-state groundwork. Frames remain byte-identical; mixed-corpus compression is currently ahead at levels 3 (+3.4%), 5 (+1.3%), 7 (+24.9%), 8 (+50.6%), 9 (+46.3%), and 15 (+26.5%), with level 1 at -4.9%. Decompression is ahead at levels 1, 5, 7, 8, 9, and 15, while level 3 is -10.4%. The generated README tables now reflect this run; row integration is not yet active, so these numbers are a baseline rather than a row-speed claim.
- After `VSStandardCollectorService150` became running, a fresh `VSDiagnostics` CPU session was attempted with the installed `CpuUsageHigh.json` agent. `CreateSession` still fails with `REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG`, confirming that the service process state does not restore the missing DiagnosticsHub COM registration; symbolized profiling remains an external installation/registration issue.
- Diagnosed the host mismatch: `VSDiagnostics.exe` is version `18.10.37531.1`, while the registered `StandardCollector.Service.exe` is version `18.5.37003.3`. The mixed DiagnosticsHub versions are the leading explanation for `REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG`; repair/update Visual Studio so the collector and client come from the same build before retrying profiling.
- Correction (2026-09-18): reverted the earlier binary-tree block-boundary tail change from 192 to 32. Reference `zstd_compress.c` explicitly uses `MIN(192, curr - nextToUpdate - 384)` before strategy dispatch. The 32-position row-matcher bound is a different operation. The previous mixed-corpus pass did not establish general parity, and candidate-versus-reference timings did not establish an improvement over the pre-change candidate.
- Tested hoisting the hash-chain parser's current-position hash across its catch-up insertion loop. Frames and Release acceptance remained exact, but three paired 300-iteration runs at levels 3 and 5 stayed within the existing noisy baseline (about 1.54–1.66 GiB/s for C++ versus 2.07–2.10 GiB/s for reference), so the hoist was reverted; MSVC's existing scheduling is preferable.
- Tested caching the current input byte used by every hash-chain candidate tag comparison; reverted. Correction: level 3 uses double-fast, so its timing movement cannot be attributed to this hash-chain change. No controlled before/after evidence establishes a register-scheduling regression.
- WSL GCC 16 Release evaluation now builds with strict warnings enabled after removing redundant casts, making bitfield truncation explicit, and renaming a shadowed sequence-table variable. The initial 100-iteration mixed-corpus run passed frame parity and showed level-3 compression at 1,500 vs 1,695 MiB/s. Other measured compression levels and all measured decompression levels led reference in this snapshot; repeated paired measurements remain required.
- WSL `perf` works with recordings on native Linux `/tmp`; recording on `/mnt/c` failed with `Bad address`. Level-3 candidate samples: double-fast parser 58.26%, sequence encoding 20.59%, separate match counter 3.40%. Reference samples: double-fast parser 53.12%, sequence encoding 13.52%, sequence-to-code conversion 5.71%. These are separate sampled runs, not direct per-function speed ratios. Next target: parser instruction-level comparison and controlled baseline/experiment timing.
- Windows AMD uProf 5.3.521 can collect both time-based and branch-counter profiles on the optimized MSVC workers. A `/O2 /Ob3 /Z7` plus `/DEBUG:FULL` level-3 build produced symbolized C++ and reference reports in `out/uprof-windows-l3-symbols/`; 3,000 frames were byte-identical. The installed Hyper-V host reports no IBS support. The first ordinary `/Zi` configure failed with MSVC C1902 (program-database manager mismatch); embedded `/Z7` debug information avoided that issue without disabling Release optimization. The C++ `encode_sequences_block` profile entry encompasses gathering, literals, table selection, and bit writing, while reference `ZSTD_encodeSequences_default` is only the final bit writer, so their sampled counts are not directly comparable.
- On the same 1-MiB mixed level-3 corpus, refreshed Release phase instrumentation measured C++ parser 947 ms and encoding 540 ms over 3,000 frames, with encoding divided into gathering 134 ms, literals 41 ms, tables 138 ms, and bits 215 ms. The reference parser measured 961 ms; total instrumented worker time was 1,630 ms C++ versus 1,766 ms reference. This directs future sequence work toward bit writing, table selection, and gathering separately, rather than treating the broad uProf encoder symbol as one bottleneck.
- Tested SSE2 16-byte match counting on the exact GCC 13 level-2, 256-KiB double-fast specialization. Six alternating 20,000-frame varied-corpus pairs were exact and 0.1–2.1% faster; reference-byte and reciprocal-decode checks passed. However, six longer 80,000-frame balanced-corpus pairs were 0.1–3.7% slower, all six in the same direction. The SIMD trial was reverted and the baseline worker SHA-256 restored. An unconditional wide comparison is not a robust replacement for the scalar counter on short-match-heavy input; future work should first quantify match-length distribution or change the parser's candidate/probe dataflow.
